DURR-FULL:v8p497/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p497/r2.claim: The Prophet rebuked Muadh for overlong prayer and directed him to recite shorter chapters, including the chapters beginning with glorification, the sun, dawn, and night.

BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r1.claim: Tasbih means declaring transcendence; some scholars say divine names are fixed by revelation, and al-A'la most clearly describes the Lord rather than the name.
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r1.anchor: التسبيح التنزيه واسم الله لا يصح أن يطلق عليه بالنظر إلى ذاته

BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r2.claim: God's height is beyond the grasp of describers and knowers, not spatial elevation or bodily size; recognizing His majesty should humble worshippers.
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم ليس علوه عو جهة ولا كبره كبر جثة سبحانه عن ذلك

BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r3.claim: The command forbids treating al-A'la as spatial height, istiwa as settling, or divine names as shared with idols and false claimants such as Musaylima.
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r3.anchor: نزه اسمه عن الإلحاد فيه بالتأويلات الزائغة نحو أن يجعل الأعلى من العلو في المكان

BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r4.claim: Reverence requires avoiding careless mention of God's name, including while yawning or relieving oneself, and careless, excessive swearing.
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r4.anchor: وكذا نزهه عن ذكره لا عى وجه الإعظام والإجلال

BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r5.speaker: جرير
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r5.claim: Jarir glosses the command as raising one's voice in remembrance of God's name, indicating that the word name is meaningful rather than redundant.
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r5.anchor: وقال جرير في الآية ارفع صوتك بذكره أي بذكر اسمه

BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r6.claim: Some commentators take name and named as one here, understanding the command to purify God's essence from imagination.
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم الاسم والمسمى هنا واحد أي نزه ذاته عما دخل في الوهم والخيال

BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r7.claim: The Prophet assigned the phrase glorify your Lord, the Magnificent to bowing and glorify your Lord, the Most High to prostration.
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r7.anchor: في الحديث لما نزلت فسبح باسم ربك العظيم قال عليه السلام اجعلوها في ركوعكم

BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r8.speaker: سعدي المفتي
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r8.claim: Sa'di al-Mufti says the hadith indicates that the word name is redundant and that saying Subhana Rabbi al-A'la fulfills the command.
BURSEVI:v10p311#3/r8.anchor: قاله سعدي المفتي وعلى أن الامتثال بالأمر يحصل بأن يقول سبحان ربي العظيم والأعلى

BURSEVI:v10p313/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p313/r1.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p313/r1.claim: Al-Qashani says the Highest and Greatest name is God's essence with all attributes; its special glorification is self-emptying until divine perfections appear.
BURSEVI:v10p313/r1.anchor: وقال القاشاني : اسمه الأعلى والأعظم هو الذات مع جميع الصفات

BURSEVI:v10p313/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p313/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p313/r2.claim: Each creature has its own form of glorification.
BURSEVI:v10p313/r2.anchor: ولك شيء تسبيح خاص يسبح به اسما خالصا

QASHANI:87:1-4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:1-4/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:1-4/r1.claim: The Highest, Greatest Name is the essence together with all attributes; glorification is the self’s stripping away everything but the Real so all divine perfections emerge, the special praise of annihilation, and each thing has a particular glorification through a particular divine name.
QASHANI:87:1-4/r1.anchor: اسمه الأعلى والأعظم هو الذات مع جميع الصفات

SULAMI:v2p389/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p389/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p389/r1.claim: The command means to declare the name of one's Lord transcendent while glorifying Him.
SULAMI:v2p389/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : نزه اسم ربك في تسبيحك له

SULAMI:v2p389/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p389/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p389/r2.claim: After remembering the Lord, keep the tongue from idle talk and lies.
SULAMI:v2p389/r2.anchor: نزه لسانك بعد ذكرك ربك عن لغو وكذب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r1.speaker: النبي محمد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r1.claim: The Prophet's reply to complaints about Muʿādh's long night prayer names this surah by its opening words; the report is in both Ṣaḥīḥs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r1.anchor: الله قال : ( قام معاذ فصلى العشاء الآخرة فطول فشكاه بعض من صلى خلفه إلى النبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r2.speaker: البراء بن عازب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r2.claim: Al-Barāʾ says he recited this surah among similar ones before the Prophet arrived in Medina; Ibn ʿĀshūr treats the report as evidence for its Meccan origin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r2.anchor: وفي ( صحيح البخاري ) عن البراء بن عازب قال : ( ما جاء رسول الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r3.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r3.claim: Al-Nuʿmān b. Bashīr reports that the Prophet recited this surah and al-Ghāshiya at Eid and Friday prayers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r3.anchor: وروى الترمذي عن النعمان بن بشير : ( أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرأ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r4.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r4.claim: ʿĀʾisha calls the surah Sabbih; her report about the Prophet's first witr rakʿah appears to use an abbreviated title rather than quote the full opening.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r4.anchor: وسمتها عائشة ( سبح ) . روى أبو داود والترمذي عنها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r5.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī and Ibn Kathīr also call it Sabbih because it uniquely opens with that imperative; most commentators and muṣḥaf writers instead call it al-Aʿlā.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r5.anchor: وسماها أكثر المفسرين وكتاب المصاحف ( سورة الأعلى ) لوقوع صفة الأعلى فيها دون غيرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r6.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r6.claim: Most authorities classify the surah as Meccan; reports from Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās make verses 14–15 Medinan, while al-Ḍaḥḥāk calls the whole surah Medinan.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r7.claim: Its subject matter supports a Meccan origin, especially the promise that God will make the Prophet recite and not forget.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r7.anchor: وما اشتملت عليه من المعاني يشهد لكونها مكية وحسبك بقوله تعالى : { سنقرئك فلا تنسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r8.speaker: جابر بن زيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r8.claim: Jābir b. Zayd ranks it eighth in revelation, after al-Takwīr and before al-Layl; Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima, and al-Ḥasan rank it seventh in an early-surah sequence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r8.anchor: وهي معدودة ثامنة في ترتيب نزول السور عند جابر بن زيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r9.claim: Jābir b. Zayd counts al-Fātiḥa after al-Muddaththir, making al-Aʿlā eighth; either order places it among the earliest surahs, supported by its promise in verse 6.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p271/r9.anchor: فهي من أوائل السور وقوله تعالى : { سنقرئك فلا تنسى ينادي على ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r1.claim: The surah selects God's description as Most High because it honors the Quran and steadies its reception; the Quran's dignity follows from being God's speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r1.anchor: وإيثار هذا الوصف في هذه السورة لأنها تضمنت التنويه بالقرآن والتثبيت على تلقيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r2.claim: Divine highness supplies the rule for interpreting God's attributes; ambiguous descriptions must be understood in a way befitting the Most High.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r2.anchor: وهذا الوصف هو ملاك القانون في تفسير صفات الله تعالى ومحاملها على ما يليق بوصف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r3.claim: The opening also gives the prostration formula سبحان ربي الأعلى, joining spoken glorification to bodily glorification.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p275/r3.anchor: وقد جعل من قوله تعالى : { سبح اسم ربك الأعلى } دعاء السجود في الصلاة

TUSTARI:87:1/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:87:1/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:87:1/r1.claim: Glorifying God means outwardly denying that He has rivals or opposites, and inwardly remembering Him in prayer while witnessing none other.
TUSTARI:87:1/r1.anchor: هو تنزيهه عن الأضداد والأنداد في الظاهر، وفي الباطن مشاهدته بالذكر في الصلاة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r1.claim: Most interpreters say sabbiḥ means to say “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r1.anchor: أحدها قل سبحان ربي الأعلى قاله الجمهور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r2.claim: A second explanation takes sabbiḥ to mean magnify the Lord.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r3.claim: Two further meanings transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās are to pray by the Lord's command and to declare Him free of evil.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r3.anchor: والثالث صل بأمر ربك روي القولان عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains sabbiḥ as declaring the Lord free of evil.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r4.anchor: والرابع نزه ربك عن السوء قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r5.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r5.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī says to sanctify God's name means remembering Him reverently and humbly.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r5.anchor: والخامس نزه اسم ربك وذكرك إياه أن تذكره وأنت معظم له خاشع له ذكره الثعلبي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r6.claim: Two explanations are offered for “the name of your Lord”: the word “name” may be an added link with no independent force, or it may be essential.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p87/r6.anchor: قولان أحدهما أن ذكر الأسم صلة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan; al-Bara's account of the early migrants reciting it before the Prophet's arrival in Medina supports this dating.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r1.anchor: والدليل على ذلك ما رواه البخاري: حدثنا عبدان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r2.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r2.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet loved this surah; Ahmad alone transmits this report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r2.anchor: عن ثوير بن أبي فاختة، عن أبيه، عن علي قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يحب هذه السورة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r3.claim: In the two Ṣaḥīḥs, the Prophet tells Muʿadh that he should have recited al-Aʿlā, al-Shams, and al-Layl in prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r3.anchor: وثبت في الصحيحين: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لمعاذ:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r4.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r4.claim: The Prophet recited al-Aʿlā and al-Ghāshiya at both Eids and, when Eid coincided with Friday, recited both; Tirmidhi notes a disputed link through Ḥabīb's father.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r4.anchor: عن حبيب بن سالم، عن أبيه، عن النعمان بن بشير: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ في العيدين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r5.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r5.claim: Tirmidhi says Ḥabīb ibn Sālim is not known to narrate from his father, while other routes transmit the report directly from Ḥabīb to al-Nuʿmān.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p377/r5.anchor: قال الترمذي: "وكذا رواه الثوري ومسعر، عن إبراهيم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378/r1.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378/r1.claim: The Prophet recited al-Aʿlā and al-Ghāshiya on Eid and Friday, sometimes reciting them together when the occasions coincided.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378/r1.anchor: ولفظ مسلم وأهل السنن: كان يقرأ في العيدين ويوم الجمعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378/r2.claim: A report from Ubay ibn Kaʿb says the Prophet recited al-Aʿlā, al-Kāfirūn, and al-Ikhlāṣ in the witr prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378/r2.anchor: أبي بن كعب، وعبد الله بن عباس، وعبد الرحمن بن أبزى، وعائشة أم المؤمنين: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقرأ في الوتر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378/r3.claim: ʿĀʾisha's version adds the two protecting surahs to the Prophet's witr recitation of al-Aʿlā, al-Kāfirūn, and al-Ikhlāṣ.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378/r4.speaker: جابر وأبو أمامة صدي بن عجلان وعبد الله بن مسعود وعمران بن حصين وعلي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378/r4.claim: The same witr-recitation report is also transmitted through these Companions, as abbreviated corroboration for the practice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378/r4.anchor: وهكذا روي هذا الحديث-من طريق-جابر وأبي أمامة صدي بن عجلان، وعبد الله بن مسعود، وعمران بن حصين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r1.speaker: عقبة بن عامر الجهني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r1.claim: The Prophet instructed worshippers to glorify God with al-ʿAẓīm in bowing and al-Aʿlā in prostration when those verses were revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r1.anchor: سمعت عقبة بن عامر الجهني لما نزلت: {فسبح باسم ربك العظيم}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r2.claim: A report raised to the Prophet says he would say Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, when reciting this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأ: {سبح اسم ربك الأعلى}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r3.speaker: أبو داود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r3.claim: Abu Dawud notes that Wakiʿ's raised version is opposed by Abu Wakiʿ and Shuʿba, who report the saying from Ibn Abbas as his own.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r3.anchor: وهكذا رواه أبو داود عن زهير بن حرب، عن وكيع، به (4) وقال: "خولف فيه وكيع، رواه أبو وكيع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r4.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r4.claim: ʿAlī said Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, when he recited al-Aʿlā.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r4.anchor: عن السدي، عن عبد خير قال: سمعت عليا قرأ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās would say the same glorification after al-Aʿlā and, at the close of al-Qiyāma, say Glory to You, indeed You can.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق الهمداني: أن ابن عباس كان إذا قرأ: {سبح اسم ربك الأعلى} يقول: سبحان ربي الأعلى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r6.claim: Qatada says it was related that the Prophet said Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, when reciting the verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p378#2/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: {سبح اسم ربك الأعلى} ذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأها، قال:

JISHUMI:v10p7371/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7371/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7371/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the sūra is Meccan; al-Ḍaḥḥāk says it is Medinan, and it is called Sūrat al-Aʿlā.
JISHUMI:v10p7371/r1.anchor: وقيل: إنها مكية، عن ابن عباس. وقيل: مدنية، عن الضحاك. وسميت سورة (الأعلى)

JISHUMI:v10p7371/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7371/r2.speaker: أبي
JISHUMI:v10p7371/r2.claim: Ubayy transmits the Prophet’s promise that reciting al-Aʿlā earns ten good deeds for each letter revealed to Abraham, Moses, and Muḥammad.
JISHUMI:v10p7371/r2.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه فيما رواه أبي: من قرأ سورة (الأعلى) أعطاه الله من الأجر

JISHUMI:v10p7371/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7371/r3.speaker: علي
JISHUMI:v10p7371/r3.claim: ʿAlī reports that the Prophet loved this sūra and that Michael was the first to say “Glory to my Lord, the Most High.”
JISHUMI:v10p7371/r3.anchor: وعن علي: كان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يحب هذه السورة (سبح اسم ربك)

JISHUMI:v10p7371/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7371/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7371/r4.claim: A report from the Prophet through Gabriel promises an immense scale-weight and forgiveness and Paradise for saying the phrase in or outside prayer.
JISHUMI:v10p7371/r4.anchor: يا جبريل، أخبرني عن ثواب من قالها في صلاته أو غير صلاته؟

JISHUMI:v10p7371/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7371/r5.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
JISHUMI:v10p7371/r5.claim: ʿUqba b. ʿĀmir reports that the Prophet assigned “Glorify the name of your Lord, the Great” to bowing and this verse to prostration; similar reports come from ʿAlī, Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Ibn al-Zubayr.
JISHUMI:v10p7371/r5.anchor: وعن عقبة بن عامر قال: لما نزل قوله: (فسبح باسم ربك العظيم)

JISHUMI:v10p7371/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7371/r6.speaker: جويبر
JISHUMI:v10p7371/r6.claim: Juwaybir reports from al-Ḍaḥḥāk that he said this phrase in prostration and directed anyone reciting the sūra to say it likewise.
JISHUMI:v10p7371/r6.anchor: وعن جويبر، عن الضحاك أنه كان يقول ذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r1.claim: To glorify God's name is to deny meanings unworthy of Him, such as compulsion or anthropomorphism; al-A'la means supremacy and power, not spatial height or literal settlement on the Throne.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r1.anchor: تنزيهه عما لا يصح فيه من المعاني

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r2.claim: Al-A'la may qualify the Lord or the name, and Ali reads the verse as Glory to my Lord, the Most High.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r2.anchor: وقرأ علي رضي الله عنه : سبحان ربي الأعلى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r3.claim: A prophetic report says that after the command to glorify the Great Lord was revealed, worshippers were told to say it in bowing; after this verse, to say it in prostration.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( اجعلوها في ركوعكم )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r5.speaker: علي وابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r5.claim: When the Prophet recited this surah he said Glory to my Lord the Most High; Ali and Ibn Abbas are also reported to say it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r5.anchor: وكان إذا قرأها قال : سبحان ربي الأعلى وكان علي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r6.claim: The source says the Prophet liked this surah and reports that Michael was the first to say Glory to my Lord the Most High.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p742#2/r6.anchor: أول من قال ( سبحان ربي الأعلى ) مكيائيل

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r1.claim: They understand sabbih as magnify your Lord; ism is an extra word intended to magnify the one named, as in Labid's poem.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r1.anchor: قاله ابن عباس والسدي , والاسم صلة قصد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r2.speaker: لبيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r2.claim: His verse is cited as poetic evidence for using ism as an extra word in praise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r2.anchor: كما قال لبيد : إلى الحول ثم اسم السلام عليكما

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r3.speaker: الطبري
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r3.claim: He interprets the command as keeping the name of the Lord from being applied to anyone else.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r3.anchor: يسمى به أحد سواه , ذكره الطبري

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r4.speaker: جرير
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r4.claim: His line supports the interpretation of sabbih as raising one's voice in remembrance of God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r4.anchor: قال جرير : قبح الإله وجوه تغلب

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r5.claim: A fourth interpretation is pray to your Lord; ism may mean by His command, by remembering Him at prayer's opening, or remembering Him in the heart when intending prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r5.anchor: في قوله ( اسم ربك ) ثلاثة أوجه : أحدها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r6.speaker: علي وابن عباس وابن عمر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r6.claim: They reportedly began reciting the sura by saying Subhana rabbi al-aʿla, acting on its opening command; Abu's recitation and Ibn Umar's reading included the formula.

MUJAHID:v2p751/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p751/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
MUJAHID:v2p751/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that when the Companions asked what to say in prostration, this verse was revealed and the Prophet instructed them to say Subhana rabbi al-a‘la an odd number of times.
MUJAHID:v2p751/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال قلنا يا رسول الله كيف نقول في سجودنا فأنزل الله عز وجل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p332/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332/r1.claim: The command means declare God's essence free of what does not befit Him; “name” is an extra word and “Most High” denotes dominion and power, not location.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332/r1.anchor: نزه ذاته عما لا يليق به والاسم صلة وذلك بأن يفسر الأعلى بمعنى العلو الذى هو القهر والافتدار

NASAFI-FULL:v4p332/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332/r2.claim: An alternative is to say “Glory be to my Lord Most High”; a report says that when this verse descended the Prophet instructed worshippers to use it in prostration.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332/r2.anchor: وقيل قل سبحان ربى الأعلى وفى الحديث لما نزلت قال علية السلام اجعلوها فى سجودكم

QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r1.claim: Readers are encouraged to say “Glory to my Lord, the Most High” after reciting the verse; the Prophet said it, as did a group of Companions and Successors.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r1.anchor: يستحب للقارىء إذا قرأ { سبح اسم ربك الأعلى } أن يقول عقبه: سبحان ربي الأعلى

QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r2.speaker: جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه عن جده
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r2.claim: A report describes an angel whose many wings could not carry him to the Throne; after God told him he could not reach even its leg, he glorified the Most High, and the Prophet said to place the phrase in prostration.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r2.anchor: لو طرت إلى نفخ الصور مع أجنحتك وقوتك لم تبلغ ساق عرشي

QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Suddi explain the command as exalting the Most High Lord; “name” is an extra word intended to exalt its referent, as in Labid’s poetic line.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والسدي: معنى { سبح اسم ربك الأعلى } أي عظم ربك الأعلى. والاسم صلة

QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r4.claim: Other explanations say to declare God free of defects and of the claims of unbelievers, or to venerate His naming and remembrance by mentioning Him reverently; the author prefers that “name” means the named one.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r4.anchor: وجعلوا الاسم بمعنى التسمية، والأولى أن يكون الاسم هو المسمى.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r5.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r5.claim: Al-Tabari says to reserve God’s name for Him and not name anyone else by it.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r5.anchor: وذكر الطبري أن المعنى نزه اسم ربك عن أن تسمي به أحدا سواه.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r6.speaker: نافع عن ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r6.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says not to say “upon God’s name,” since God’s name is the Most High.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r6.anchor: روى نافع عن ابن عمر قال: لا تقل على اسم الله فإن اسم الله هو الأعلى.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r7.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r7.claim: Abu Salih transmits Ibn ʿAbbas’s reading as “pray by the command of your Most High Lord,” meaning say the glorification.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r7.anchor: وروى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس: صل بأمر ربك الأعلى. قال: وهو أن تقول سبحان ربك الأعلى.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r8.speaker: علي وابن عباس وابن عمر وابن الزبير وأبو موسى وابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r8.claim: These Companions said the glorification when beginning the sura’s recitation; it is a recommended response, not Quran, despite a claim by some heretics and a reported Ubayy reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1/r8.anchor: وروي عن علي رضي الله عنه، وابن عباس وابن عمر وابن الزبير وأبي موسى وعبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنهم: أنهم كانوا إذا افتتحوا قراءة هذه السورة قالوا: سبحان ربي الأعلى

QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r1.claim: A report says the Prophet recited the verse and then said “Glory to my Lord, the Most High”; when Ali did so, he explained that he was obeying an instruction, not adding Quran.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r1.anchor: قال: لا، إنما أمرنا بشيء فقلته، وعن عقبة بن عامر الجهني قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r2.claim: ʿUqba ibn ʿAmir reports that when the verse was revealed, the Prophet commanded them to use it in prostration.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r2.anchor: لما نزلت { سبح اسم ربك الأعلى } قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «اجعلوها في سجودكم»

QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r3.claim: These reports indicate that “name” means the named one, since the worshippers said “Glory to my Lord,” not “Glory to my Lord’s name.”
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r3.anchor: وهذا كله يدل على أن الاسم هو المسمى لأنهم لم يقولوا: سبحان اسم ربي الأعلى.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r4.claim: One view says Michael was first to say the glorification; another hadith promises enormous reward and forgiveness for any believer who says it in or outside prayer, with Michael interceding after death.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r4.anchor: ما من مؤمن ولا مؤمنة يقولها في سجوده أو في غير سجوده

QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r5.claim: Hasan says the verse means pray to the Most High Lord; others say pray with God’s names rather than pagan whistling and clapping, or raise the voice in remembrance, as in Jarir’s poem.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:1#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: { سبح اسم ربك الأعلى } أي صل لربك الأعلى. وقيل: أي صل بأسماء الله، لا كما يصلي المشركون

NAHHAS:v5p203/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r1.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p203/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says both sabbiḥ isma rabbika and sabbiḥ bi-ismi rabbika are sound.
NAHHAS:v5p203/r1.anchor: قال الفراء سبح اسم ربك وسبح باسم ربك كل صواب

NAHHAS:v5p203/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p203/r2.claim: If al-Farrāʾ means deleting the preposition, the construction is invalid; if he means transitivity with or without a preposition, the senses still differ.
NAHHAS:v5p203/r2.anchor: إن كان قدر هذا على حذف الباء فلا يجوز مررت زيدا وإن كان قدره مما يتعدى بحرف

NAHHAS:v5p203/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p203/r3.claim: With bi-, the command means to perform glorification using the Lord's name, unlike the interpretations of sabbiḥ isma rabbika.
NAHHAS:v5p203/r3.anchor: لأن معنى سبح باسم ربك ليكن تسبيحك باسم ربك

NAHHAS:v5p203/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r4.speaker: بعضهم
NAHHAS:v5p203/r4.claim: One interpretation is to purify and exalt the Supreme Lord's name above the claims of polytheists, since He is the conqueror above all.
NAHHAS:v5p203/r4.anchor: منهم من قال معناه نزه اسم ربك الأعلى وعظمه عن أن تنسبه إلى ما نسبه إليه المشركون

NAHHAS:v5p203/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r5.speaker: بعضهم
NAHHAS:v5p203/r5.claim: Another interpretation forbids calling the idols al-ʿUzzā and al-Lāt, names derived respectively from al-ʿAzīz and Allah.
NAHHAS:v5p203/r5.anchor: ومنهم من قال أي لا تقل العزى لأنها مشتقة من العزيز ولا اللات لأنهم اشتقوا من من قولهم الله

NAHHAS:v5p203/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r6.speaker: بعضهم
NAHHAS:v5p203/r6.claim: Another interpretation is to remember the Lord's name while honoring Him with reverence and humility.
NAHHAS:v5p203/r6.anchor: ومنهم من قال معنى سبح اسم ربك أي اذكر اسم ربك وأنت معظم له خاشع متذلل

NAHHAS:v5p203/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r7.speaker: بعضهم
NAHHAS:v5p203/r7.claim: Another interpretation is to glorify the Lord's name in prayer with humble concentration.
NAHHAS:v5p203/r7.anchor: ومنهم من قال معناه سبح اسم ربك في صلاتك متخشعا مشغولا بها

NAHHAS:v5p203/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p203/r8.claim: The first explanation is clearest; Ibn ʿAbbās reports that whenever the Prophet recited this verse he said, Glory to my Lord, the Most High.
NAHHAS:v5p203/r8.anchor: والجواب الأول أبينها كما قرىء على محمد بن جعفر عن يوسف بن موسى عن وكيع

NAHHAS:v5p203/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p203/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports the Prophet's practice of saying subḥāna rabbī al-aʿlā after reciting the verse.
NAHHAS:v5p203/r9.anchor: عن مسلم البطين عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قرأ ( سبح اسم ربك الأعلى ) قال سبحان ربي الأعلى الأعلى في موضع خفض

NAHHAS:v5p203/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p203/r10.claim: Al-aʿlā is genitive as an adjective of rabb or ism, and the author prefers its attachment to rabb.
NAHHAS:v5p203/r10.anchor: الأعلى في موضع خفض نعت لربك أو لاسم والأولى أن يكون نعتا لما عليه

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.claim: Al-Aʿla is Meccan and has nineteen verses; the Prophet loved it, recited it at Eid and Friday prayers with al-Ghashiya, sometimes on the same day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.anchor: سورة الأعلى مكية وآياتها تسع عشرة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet loved this surah; Muslim reports that he recited it with al-Ghashiya at Eid and on Friday, sometimes reciting both on one day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.anchor: أن رسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] كان يحب هذه السورة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.claim: The surah turns the entire cosmos into a sanctuary reverberating with praise and offers the Prophet good news of divine preservation and ease in his mission and affairs.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.anchor: وحق لرسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أن يحب هذه السورة وهي تحيل له الكون كله معبدا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.claim: Its foundations are God's oneness as creator, divine revelation, and afterlife recompense, rooted in earlier scriptures; it also portrays the easy nature of the message, messenger, and community.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.anchor: وهي تتضمن الثابت من قواعد التصور الإيماني

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r5.claim: The opening's relaxed, extended rhythm releases echoes of glorification and displays the Creator's work throughout existence.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r5.anchor: ليطلق في الجو ابتداء أصداء التسبيح

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r6.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r6.claim: Tasbih is exaltation and declaring God transcendent, with inward awareness and lived experience of His beautiful attributes, rather than merely repeating “Subhan Allah.”
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r6.anchor: والتسبيح هو التمجيد والتنزيه واستحضار معاني الصفات الحسنى لله

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r7.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r7.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r7.claim: Rabb means nurturer and caretaker, a tender shade fitting the surah; al-Aʿla directs the spirit toward endless horizons and coheres with exaltation.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r7.anchor: والصفة الأولى القريبة في هذا النص هي صفة الرب . وصفة الأعلى . . والرب : المربي والراعي

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r8.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r8.claim: The Prophet responded directly to the command by reciting “Glory to my Lord Most High,” embodying immediate closeness and obedience.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r8.anchor: وقد كان رسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] يقرأ هذا الأمر

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r9.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r9.claim: When this verse descended, the Prophet instructed worshippers to include its glorification in prostration; when 56:74 descended, he assigned that verse to bowing.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r9.anchor: وحينما نزلت هذه الآية قال :  "  اجعلوها في سجودكم  "

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r10.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r10.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r10.claim: Permission to praise and connect with God is itself a divine favor, given in a form people can grasp and glimpse of His attributes.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r10.anchor: فإذن الله لعباده بأن يحمدوه ويسبحوه إحدى نعمه عليهم وأفضاله

RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r1.claim: The command may mean glorifying God's name itself, or treating 'name' as an added word and glorifying God directly.
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r1.anchor: في قوله : { اسم ربك } قولان : أحدهما : أن المراد

RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r2.claim: One reading forbids giving God's name to anyone else, as idolaters called an idol al-Lat and Musaylima 'the Merciful of Yamama.'
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r2.anchor: نزه اسم ربك عن أن تسمي به غيره

RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r3.claim: Another reading rejects interpreting divine names in ways that imply place or bodily settling, and instead construes exaltation as power and mastery.
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r3.anchor: أن يفسر الأعلى بالعلو في المكان والاستواء بالاستقرار

RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r4.claim: A further reading prohibits treating God's names casually or uttering them without reverence and awareness of their meanings.
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r4.anchor: أن يصان عن الابتذال والذكر لا على وجه الخشوع والتعظيم

RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation says to glorify God using the revealed names alone, invoking them as prayer rather than using the polytheists' ritual clapping and whistling.
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r5.anchor: مجده بأسمائه التي أنزلتها عليك وعرفتك أنها أسماؤه

RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r6.claim: Al-Farra sees no difference between 'glorify the name of your Lord' and 'glorify by the name'; al-Wahidi distinguishes them as glorifying the name versus God through a name.
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r6.anchor: قال الفراء : لا فرق بين { سبح اسم ربك } وبين { فسبح باسم ربك }

RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r7.claim: Abu Muslim says 'name' here means attribute, as it does in the command to call upon God by His beautiful names.
RAZI-FULL:v31p123#2/r7.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : المراد من الاسم ههنا الصفة

RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r1.claim: Labid uses a line to show that the expression name of peace can mean peace itself, a familiar Arabic convention.
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r1.anchor: إلى الحول ثم اسم السلام عليكما

RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r2.claim: On that reading, praising God includes avoiding conduct that provokes unbelievers to insult God and declaring Him free of all imperfections in essence, attributes, acts, names, and judgments.
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r2.anchor: أنه عبارة عن تنزيه الله تعالى عن كل ما لا يليق به

RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r3.claim: In the author's theology, God's essence is neither substance nor accident, His attributes are uncreated and perfect, and His actions are those of the absolute owner who cannot be challenged.
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r3.anchor: أما في ذاته فأن يعتقد أنها ليست من الجواهر والأعراض

RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r4.claim: The Mu'tazilites say God's acts are all good and He neither does nor approves evil; they define divine names as words implying no deficiency, even if not revealed.
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r4.anchor: وقالت المعتزلة هو أن يعتقد أن كل ما فعله فهو صواب حسن

RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r5.claim: On divine commands, the author says God imposes no duty for His own benefit but from sovereign ownership, whereas the Mu'tazilites say duties serve human welfare.
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r5.anchor: بل إما لمحض المالكية على ما هو قولنا

RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r6.claim: The claim that name and named are identical is ill-framed: if name means a word and named means the entity they differ, while if both mean the entity the claim is a tautology.
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r6.anchor: فالعاقل لا يمكنه أن يقول : الاسم هو المسمى

RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r7.claim: A subtle linguistic reason for confusion is that the word 'name' is itself a name, which could have led early scholars to generalize identity between names and named things.
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r7.anchor: يلزم أن يكون الاسم إسما لنفسه

RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p124/r8.claim: The argument that one cannot say 'glory to the name of God' and therefore the name is God Himself is weak because the verse allows several readings, including glorifying the name or glorifying God by it.

RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r1.claim: Uqba ibn Amir reports that the Prophet directed Muslims to say 'glorified is my Lord, the Great' in bowing after 56:74, and 'glorified is my Lord, the Highest' in prostration after 87:1.
RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r1.anchor: روى عن عقبة بن عامر أنه لما نزل قوله تعالى : { فسبح باسم ربك العظيم }

RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r2.claim: Ali and Ibn Umar reportedly recited an explicit 'Glory to my Lord, the Highest' after the command, supplying the commanded glorification.
RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r2.anchor: قرأ علي عليه السلام وابن عمر : سبحان ربي الأعلى

RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r3.claim: The corporealists cite 'the Highest' for spatial height, but the author argues that God cannot be spatially above creation: finite or infinite dimensions each entail impossibility.
RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r3.anchor: والحق أن العلو بالجهة على الله تعالى محال

RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r4.claim: The surrounding context favors exalted power rather than location: spatial distance would not establish worthiness of praise, while creating and proportioning demonstrate power.
RAZI-FULL:v31p125/r4.anchor: والخالقية تناسب العلو بحسب القدرة لا العلو بحسب الجهة

RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r1.claim: The objection that 'Great' and 'Highest' imply two gods fails because God's oneness is established and the verse never says He is higher than another lord.
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r1.anchor: هذه الآية أنه سبحانه وتعالى أعلى من رب آخر

RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r2.claim: 'The Highest' can mean God's grandeur surpasses every description, remembrance, human gratitude, and act of obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r2.anchor: أعلى وأجل وأعظم من كل ما يصفه به الواصفون

RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r3.claim: The title also indicates that God deserves transcendence from every defect, being highest by sovereignty, authority, and power; alternatively it means simply 'high,' as 'greater' can mean 'great.'
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r3.anchor: العالي على كل شيء بملكه وسلطانه وقدرته

RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r4.claim: A report says the Prophet loved this surah and said anyone who knew its merit would repeat it sixteen times.
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r4.anchor: روي أنه عليه السلام كان يحب هذه السورة ويقول

RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r5.claim: Aisha heard a Bedouin add a rhymed passage about pregnancy and resurrection to the surah; she rebuked him and prayed that he and his household not return safely.
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r5.anchor: أن عائشة مرت بأعرابي يصلي بأصحابه فقرأ

SAMIN-DURR:87:1/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:1/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:1/r1.claim: Al-aʿlā may be genitive as an adjective of rabb or accusative as an adjective of ism; choosing the latter forces alladhī to modify ism or stand detached, avoiding separation from rabb by another adjective.

STUDYQURAN:87:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:1/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:1/r1.claim: Most commentators attach Most High to Lord, making the verse an injunction to glorify God; attaching it to Name instructs worshippers not to associate other things with God’s Name or to praise Him with revealed Names.
STUDYQURAN:87:1/r1.anchor: The Most High can be understood to modify Lord or the Name, though most prefer the former

STUDYQURAN:87:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:1/r2.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
STUDYQURAN:87:1/r2.claim: When 56:74 was revealed the Prophet instructed companions to enact it while bowing; for this verse he instructed them to enact it while prostrating.
STUDYQURAN:87:1/r2.anchor: when the present verse was revealed, he said, “Enact it when you prostrate”

STUDYQURAN:87:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:1/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:1/r3.claim: Muslims recite Glory be to God, the Magnificent three times in bowing and Glory be to God, the Most High three times in prostration.
STUDYQURAN:87:1/r3.anchor: Muslims thus say “Glory be to God, the Magnificent” three times when bowing in prayer

TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar recited the verse followed by “Glory to my Lord, the Most High,” and said this also occurred in Ubayy’s reading.
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر، أنه كان يقرأ: " (سبح اسم ربك الأعلى سبحان ربي الأعلى الذي خلق فسوى) قال: وهي في قراءة أبي بن كعب كذلك "

TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r2.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r2.claim: ʿAlī recited “Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High” and then said “Glory to my Lord, the Most High.”
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r2.anchor: عن عبد خير، قال: سمعت عليا، رضي الله عنه قرأ: {سبح اسم ربك الأعلى} [الأعلى: 1] فقال: سبحان ربي الأعلى

TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās would say “Glory to my Lord, the Most High” after reciting the verse.
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r3.anchor: أن ابن عباس، كان إذا قرأ: {سبح اسم ربك الأعلى} [الأعلى: 1] يقول: سبحان ربي الأعلى

TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r4.speaker: قتادة عن النبي
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r4.claim: Qatāda reports that the Prophet would say “Glory to my Lord, the Most High” when reciting this verse.
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، " {سبح اسم ربك الأعلى} [الأعلى: 1] ذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأها قال: سبحان ربي الأعلى "

TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r5.claim: One interpretation tells Muhammad not to apply the Most High Lord’s name to anything else, as idolaters named their idols al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā.
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك: نزه يا محمد اسم ربك الأعلى، أن تسمي به شيئا سواه

TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r6.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r6.claim: Another interpretation says to declare God free of what the polytheists say, connecting the command with the prohibition against insulting their deities.
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r6.anchor: وقال غيرهم: بل معنى ذلك: نزه الله عما يقول فيه المشركون كما قال:

TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r7.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r7.claim: A further interpretation takes “name” as the act of naming: mention the Lord only with humble submission.
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: نزه تسميتك يا محمد ربك الأعلى وذكرك إياه، أن تذكره إلا وأنت له خاشع متذلل

TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r8.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r8.claim: Another view understands the command as praying while remembering the Lord and being reverently fearful of Him.
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r8.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى قوله: {سبح اسم ربك الأعلى} [الأعلى: 1] : صل بذكر ربك يا محمد

TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r9.claim: Ṭabarī prefers glorifying and sanctifying the Lord’s name so it is not used to invoke idols; the transmitted practice of saying “Glory to my Lord, the Most High” supports that meaning.
TAB-FULL:v24p309#2/r9.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك عندنا بالصواب: قول من قال: معناه: نزه اسم ربك أن تدعو به الآلهة والأوثان

TABATABAI:87:14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:14/r2.claim: The opening command glorifies God by purifying His name in speech: do not associate gods, partners, or intercessors, attribute divine acts to others, or ascribe defects to God.
TABATABAI:87:14/r2.anchor: تنزيهه أن لا يذكر معه ما هو تعالى منزه عنه كذكر الآلهة والشركاء والشفعاء

TABATABAI:87:14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:14/r3.claim: Purifying God’s name in speech corresponds to purifying Him in action and entails complete monotheism, as illustrated by the reaction to mentioning God alone.
TABATABAI:87:14/r3.anchor: وهو تنزيهه تعالى في مرحلة القول الموافق لتنزيهه في مرحلة الفعل

TABATABAI:87:17-19/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r5.claim: Uqba ibn ʿĀmir al-Juhanī reports that the Prophet instructed Muslims to recite the glorification of the Most High in prostration; the author notes corroborating collections.
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r5.anchor: بحث روائي في تفسير العياشي عن عقبة بن عامر الجهني قال لما نزلت { فسبح باسم ربك العظيم } قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:87:17-19/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r6.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r6.claim: Al-Qummī glosses the command as saying “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.”
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r6.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي { سبح اسم ربك الأعلى } قال قل سبحان ربي الأعلى

ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r1.claim: Sabbih means to declare the Lord free of evil and to say subḥāna rabbī al-aʿlā.
ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r1.anchor: أي نزه ربك عن السوء وقل:

TABRISI:87:7-9/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7-9/r5.claim: Al-aʿlā is like al-akbar: supreme in power and authority, without implying that God occupies a place.
TABRISI:87:7-9/r5.anchor: الأعلى نظير الأكبر ومعناه العالي بسلطانه وقدرته وكل من دونه في سلطانه ولا يقتضي ذلك المكان

TABRISI:87:7-9/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7-9/r11.claim: Al-aʿlā may grammatically modify Lord in the genitive or name in the accusative.
TABRISI:87:7-9/r11.anchor: الأعلى يحتمل أن يكون جرا صفة لرب وأن يكون نصبا صفة لاسم

TABRISI:87:7/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r1.speaker: الباقر
TABRISI:87:7/r1.claim: Al-Bāqir advises the reciter to say “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High,” even silently during prayer.
TABRISI:87:7/r1.anchor: قال الباقر ع: إذا قرأت { سبح اسم ربك الأعلى } فقل سبحان ربي الأعلى

TABRISI:87:7/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7/r2.claim: Al-aʿlā means the all-capable one, with no one more capable, who overpowers everyone.
TABRISI:87:7/r2.anchor: والأعلى معناه القادر الذي لا قادر أقدر منه القاهر لكل أحد

TABRISI:87:7/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7/r3.claim: Another interpretation makes al-aʿlā an adjective of the name: glorify God by His highest name, since all His beautiful names are highest.
TABRISI:87:7/r3.anchor: الأعلى صفة الاسم والمعنى سبح الله بذكر اسمه الأعلى وأسماؤه الحسنى كلها أعلى

TABRISI:87:7/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:87:7/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also glosses the command as praying in the name of the Most High Lord.
TABRISI:87:7/r4.anchor: معناه صل باسم ربك الأعلى عن ابن عباس

THALABI:v10p183#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p183#2/r1.speaker: جماعة من الصحابة والتابعين
THALABI:v10p183#2/r1.claim: A group of Companions and Successors understands the command as saying ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.’
THALABI:v10p183#2/r1.anchor: يعني قل: سبحان ربي الأعلى، وإلى هذا التأويل ذهب جماعة من الصحابة والتابعين

THALABI:v10p183#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p183#2/r2.speaker: قوم
THALABI:v10p183#2/r2.claim: Some take the command to mean declaring God above the claims of deniers and false describers, treating ‘name’ as an extra word.
THALABI:v10p183#2/r2.anchor: وقال قوم معناه: نزه ربك الأعلى عما يقول فيه الملحدون ويصفه به المبطلون

THALABI:v10p183#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p183#2/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p183#2/r3.claim: It may mean declaring God's essence free of what does not befit it, since name, essence, and self all refer to existence and affirmation.
THALABI:v10p183#2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون معناه، نزه ذات ربك عما لا يليق به، لأن الاسم والذات والنفس

THALABI:v10p183#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p183#2/r4.speaker: آخرون
THALABI:v10p183#2/r4.claim: Others understand it as revering God's designation and remembrance, speaking of Him only with humility and respect; ‘name’ means the act of naming.
THALABI:v10p183#2/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: نزه تسمية ربك وذكرك إياه إن تذكره إلا وأنت خاشع معظم

THALABI:v10p183#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p183#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v10p183#2/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says sabbiḥ is equivalent to sabbiḥ bi-ismi when remembrance and glorification are intended.
THALABI:v10p183#2/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء: سواء قلت سبح اسم ربك أو سبح باسم ربك إذا أردت ذكره وتسبيحه

THALABI:v10p183#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p183#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p183#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets it as praying at the command of the Most High Lord.
THALABI:v10p183#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: صل بأمر ربك الأعلى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says sabbiḥ isma rabbika and fasabbiḥ bi-isimi rabbik both occur in Arabic with the same meaning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r1.anchor: قال الفراء: "سبح اسم ربك"، و" [فسبح] باسم ربك (¬2)، كل ذلك قد جاء، وهو كلام العرب (¬3).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r2.claim: The author distinguishes them: sabbiḥ bi-ismi rabbik glorifies God by mentioning the name that declares His transcendence above what wrongdoers say.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r2.anchor: هذا كلامه، وكأنة جعلهما (¬4) بمعنى واحد، وبينهما فرق؛ لأن معنى "سبح باسم ربك" نزه الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r3.claim: Sabbiḥ isma rabbik instead means declare the name free of defect, or say Subḥāna rabbī al-aʿlā, as exegetes explain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r3.anchor: و"سبح اسم ربك" (نزهه من السوء، وقيل: سبحان ربي الأعلى) (¬6)، # وهذا معنى قول المفسرين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r4.speaker: علي وابن عباس وابن الزبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r4.claim: Reports from ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Ibn al-Zubayr say they recited the verse and said Subḥāna rabbī al-aʿlā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r4.anchor: وقد روى عن علي (¬2)، وابن عباس (¬3)، وابن الزبير (¬4) (¬5) -رضي الله عنهم- أنهم قرؤوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r5.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r5.claim: The author of al-Naẓm uses the phrase to argue that name and named referent are one: one glorifies the name of God by glorifying God, since a name itself cannot be the object of glorification if distinct.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p429#2/r5.anchor: قال صاحب النظم: قد احتج بهذا الفصل من يقول: إن الاسم، والمسمى واحد؛ لأن أحدا لا يقول:

WAHIDI-QT:87:1/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:1/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:87:1/r1.claim: The command means to declare God's essence exalted above every defect.

WAHIDI-QT:87:1/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:1/r2.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-QT:87:1/r2.claim: Another explanation is to say, “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.”
WAHIDI-QT:87:1/r2.anchor: وقيل معناه قل سبحان ربي الأعلى

ELMALILI:87:1/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:1/r1.claim: Elmalılı renders the command as glorifying the name of one's Lord, the Most High.
ELMALILI:87:1/r1.anchor: Meâl: Tesbih et Rabbinin a‘lâ ismine

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r1.claim: Elmalılı reads the command as declaring the nurturing Lord above all and purifying His beautiful names, including al-Aʿlā, from every unworthy meaning.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r1.anchor: Rabbinin a‘lâ ismini tesbih ile tenzih et yani seni yetiştiren

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r2.claim: Names unique to God's essence or attributes belong only to Him; names describing divine acts must also be understood free of low, creaturely implications and recalled reverently.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r2.anchor: O’nun zâten ve sıfaten kendisine mahsus olan Allah, er-Rahmân, Hallâk, Rezzâk

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r3.claim: After 86:15–17, recalling the Lord's supremacy assures the Prophet that God's promise will prevail over the disbelievers' plotting and delay, and calls him to gratitude.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r3.anchor: et-Târık 86/15-17] buyurulması akibinde burada böyle ism-i Rabb’in a‘lâ olduğunun ihtârı

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r4.claim: Some call “name” redundant, mean the named referent, or identify name and referent; Elmalılı says these views all intend sanctification of the referent through its name.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r4.anchor: bazıları da isim müsemmânın aynıdır demiş iseler de hepsinin murâdı

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r5.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains glorifying God's name as freeing it from invalid meanings such as anthropomorphism and protecting its mention from casual, irreverent use.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r5.anchor: Sâhib-Keşşâf da تَسْبِيحُ اسْمِهِ تَعَالَى: تَنْزِيهُهُ عَمَّا لاَ يَصِحُّ فِيهِ مِنَ الْمَعَانِي

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r6.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r6.claim: Ukba b. Amir reports that the Prophet directed the believers to say the great Lord's tasbih in bowing and this surah's tasbih in prostration.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r6.anchor: Ukbe b. Âmir-i Cühenî’den rivayet etmişlerdir, demiştir ki

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r7.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that whenever the Prophet recited this verse, he said “Subhana rabbi al-aʿla.”
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r7.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan rivayet etmişlerdir ki Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r8.claim: The wording might have been “glorify by the name” as in the other verse, but the direct object “name” deliberately signals that the name itself is also to be sanctified.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r8.anchor: Buna nazaran فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظ۪يمِ denildiği gibi burada da

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r9.claim: Al-Aʿlā can qualify either the Lord or His name; it is explanatory, since there is no other Lord, while divine names have ranks yet all are beautiful and exalted.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r9.anchor: ٱلْأَعْلَى “Rabb”in de, “ism”in de vasfı olabilir; ihtirâzî değil, kâşifedir

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r10.claim: The exaltedness intended is not spatial height but superiority in perfection of power, effects, strength, and judgments.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r10.anchor: “ulüv”den murad mekânî yükseklik değil, kudret ve âsârda, kuvvet ve ahkâmda ekmeliyet

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r11.claim: Tasbih may be spoken purification, marked by “Subhanallah,” or practical worship: inward belief in unity and acts such as prayer, jihad, and enjoining right and forbidding wrong.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r11.anchor: Tesbîh-i kavlî lisânen yapılan tenzih ve takdistir ki سُبْحَانَ الله demek bunun alemi olmuştur

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r12.claim: Tasbih also conventionally means prayer, especially voluntary prayer; reading it here as prayer “by the Lord's name” would require an elided preposition, which Elmalılı calls contrary to the apparent wording.

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r13.speaker: İsâmuddin
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r13.claim: Alusi reports Isamuddin's suggestion that “name” can mean God's effects, since creation points to its maker as a name does.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r13.anchor: Âlûsî’nin nakline göre İsâmuddin demiştir ki: “‘İsm’ ile murad eser olmak da ba‘îd değildir

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r14.claim: Elmalılı finds the effects reading strained because no contextual clue displaces the familiar meaning of “name,” though the following attributes resemble the proposed interpretation.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r14.anchor: “ism”in mâruf olan mânasını mâni‘bir karîne olmadığı hâlde zarûretsiz bir tevil gibi görünür

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r15.claim: The effects reading does not mean creation is independently flawless; it forbids faulting it insofar as it is God's work and sign, returning to divine creative attributes and the universal glorification in 17:44.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r15.anchor: maksad mahlûkātın kendilerine nazaran bizzat kendilerini tenzih değil, tasrih olunduğu üzere Allah teâlâ’nın mahlûku olmaları

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r16.speaker: Şeyh Abduh
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r16.claim: Abduh defines God's name here as whatever enables people to know Him: minds recognize Him through attributes such as knowledge, power, and wisdom as disclosed in creation.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r16.anchor: Şeyh Abduh İsam’ın bu fikrini şu suretle ifade ederek yegâne bir mâna gibi göstermiş

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r17.speaker: Şeyh Abduh
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r17.claim: Abduh links this sense of “name” with the divine “face” in 55:27–78 and Adam being taught the names in 2:31; these are the forms by which beings or God are known.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r17.anchor: kavlinde mezkur olan esmâ da bu mânaca isimdendir

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r18.speaker: Şeyh Abduh
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r18.claim: On Abduh's reading, sanctifying God's name excludes likeness to creation, indwelling in a creature, partners, offspring, and other unworthy defects; the next verses identify Him as Creator and Guide.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r18.anchor: Biz O’na akıllarımızı ancak şöyle tevcih ederiz: O her şeyin hâlıkıdır

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r19.claim: Abduh's account broadens a name's conventional linguistic indication to rational and natural signs, a valid metaphor when it does not sanctify the world itself; nevertheless, leaving the apparent meaning is remote.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r19.anchor: bunun hâsılı, “isim”de muteber olan delâlet-i vaz‘iyeyi, delâlet-i akliye ve tabî‘iyeye ta‘mîm etmektir

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r20.claim: In the Sufi account, essence is described by attributes, names are the attributes, and effects are consequences of names, not the names themselves; the sanctified referent is God's essence.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r20.anchor: Sûfiyye mizâcınca da sıfât zâtın, esmâ sıfâtın, âsâr esmânın muktezâsı olan ahkâmı olduğuna göre

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r21.claim: Sanctifying God's essence through His name is apt because speech expresses its purity by pure names, while human minds know the divine essence only through names, attributes, or effects; direct manifestation is an afterlife matter.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r21.anchor: zât-ı baht bizim dünyada ukūl ve ezhânımızın doğrudan doğru teveccüh ve idrâkinden çok yüksek

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r22.claim: Although “name” can broadly include verbal, rational, and natural indications that turn the mind toward God, its clearest ordinary sense is the linguistic names and attributes conveyed in revelation.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r22.anchor: tam mânasıyla mütebâdir olan hakikat bize müsemmâlarını lisânî suretler

ELMALILI:87:1#2/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r23.claim: The choice “your Lord, the Most High” signals why He must be sanctified; the following attributes explain and establish this lordship and exaltedness.
ELMALILI:87:1#2/r23.anchor: tesbih ve tenzih emrinin vechine işaret olmak üzere “rabbike’l-a‘lâ” ismi ihtar olunmuş

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r1.claim: The praise sense of sabbaḥa is not explicable from Arabic sabaḥa, swim or glide, and likely reflects semantic influence from Syriac šabbeḥ, as ṣallā for prayer reflects Syriac ṣloṯā.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r1.anchor: im I. Stamm bedeutet „schwimmen, dahingleiten“) und dürfte auf semantische Interferenz von syrisch šabbeḥ zurückzuführen sein

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r2.claim: Syriac šabbeḥ translates Hebrew hillel, so the imperative echoes the psalmic call hallelû yāh; the psalms also praise God’s name as in this verse.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r2.anchor: so dass in dem Imperativ sabbiḥi sma rabbika letzten Endes der psalmische Aufruf hallelû yāh, „Lobet den Herrn!“

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r3.speaker: Muʿǧam
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r3.claim: A variant reading is subḥāna rabbiya l-aʿlā, but the author retains the common imperative reading because similar imperatives open other early Meccan texts.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Überliefert wird auch die Variante subḥāna rabbiya l-ʾaʿlā

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r4.claim: The invocation of God’s name recurs in early Meccan Quran passages and has a prominent biblical precedent, where the divine name is praised.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r4.anchor: Der „Name Gottes“ ist bereits in der biblischen Literatur prominent

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r5.claim: Al-aʿlā parallels Hebrew elyôn as a divine epithet, but Quranic al-aʿlā is an attribute following rabb plus a possessive suffix; YHWH elyôn is the closest biblical construction.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:1:anmerkung/r5.anchor: Auch das koranische al-ʾaʿlā fungiert als Attribut und erscheint bezogen auf Gott immer nach rabb + Possesivsuffix

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r2.claim: The neighboring calls to praise and admonish may share a setting with other early Meccan passages; the likely setting is Mecca’s Kaʿba cult, not private devotions of an already constituted community.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:9-15:kommentar/r2.anchor: Die Nachbarschaft der beiden Aufrufe in V. 1 und V. 9 legt, wie auch andere frühmekkanische Texte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r1.claim: Tasbih means declaring God free of names, qualities, and acts unworthy of Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r1.anchor: Tesbîh, Allah’ı kendisine lâyık olmayan isimlerden, niteliklerden ve eylemlerden tenzih etmek

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#3/r1.claim: When Ibn ʿAbbās recited this verse, he would say, ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.’
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367#3/r1.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق عن سعيد بن جبير قال كان ابن عباس إذا قرأ

ALUSI-FULL:v30p102/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102/r1.claim: Alusi reads the command as revering God's names: do not force an interpretation without need, affirm an impossible literal meaning, apply a unique divine name to another, or use it in a way that equates God with others; avoid vulgar or irreverent settings and speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102/r1.anchor: سبح اسم ربك الأعلى أي نزه أسماءه عز وجل عما لا يليق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p102/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102/r2.speaker: مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102/r2.claim: Malik would tell a rejected petitioner simply that he had nothing to give, rather than invoking God, because he would not mention God's name to someone who disliked hearing it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102/r2.anchor: وعن الإمام مالك رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه كان إذا لم يجد ما يعطي السائل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p102/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102/r3.claim: This first reading assumes “name” is not an inserted word; many instead treat it as an insertion that magnifies the divine referent, as in Labid's verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102/r3.anchor: وما ذكر من التفسير مبني على الظاهر من أن لفظ اسم غير مقحم وذهب كثير إلى أنه مقحم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r1.speaker: عقبة بن عامر الجهني
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r1.claim: After the command to glorify God's great name was revealed, the Prophet told the Companions to use it in bowing; when the command to glorify the Most High came, he told them to use it in prostration.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r1.anchor: عن عقبة بن عامر الجهني قال لما نزلت فسبح باسم ربك العظيم قال لنا رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r2.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that when the Prophet recited this verse he said “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.”
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأ سبح اسم ربك الأعلى قال سبحان ربي الأعلى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r3.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r3.claim: When ʿAli said “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High” in prayer, he answered a question about adding to the Qur'an by explaining that he was merely carrying out the command.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r3.anchor: أن عليا كرم الله تعالى وجهه قرأ ذلك فقال سبحان ربي الأعلى وهو في الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r4.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the command as protecting God's names from heretical meanings such as determinism and anthropomorphism, as well as vulgarity and irreverent use.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r4.anchor: وفي الكشاف تسبيح اسمه تعالى تنزيهه عما لا يصح فيه من المعاني التي هي إلحاد في أسمائه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r5.claim: Alusi says words used for divine names must be protected from obscenity and bad manners, and discusses criticism of Ibn al-Farid's poetic use of “Layla” and “Naʿm.”
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r5.anchor: قال الإمام أنه كما يجب تنزيه ذاته تعالى وصفاته جلى وعلا عن النقائض يجب تنزيه الألفاظ الموضوعة لذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r6.claim: Alusi discusses Ibn al-Farid poetry using Layla and Naʿm, criticized as irreverent, and a defense that treats the lines as allusive extended metaphor.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p102#2/r6.anchor: ومن هذا يعلم ما في التعبير عنه تعالى شأنه بنحو ليلى ونعم كما يدعى ذلك في قول ابن الفارض قدس سره أبرق بدا من جانب الغور لامع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r1.claim: The phrase may mean “naming of your Lord”: mention Him with reverence and treat His remembrance as honored.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r1.anchor: وقال الاسم بمعنى التسمية والمعنى نزه تسمية ربك بأن تذكره وأنت له سبحانه معظم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r2.claim: A defense of such poetry treats it as an extended metaphor with no word-by-word comparison; Alusi reports that critics reject this defense, while noting metaphorical allegory is used even for the basmala.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r2.anchor: والأظهر أن يقال إن الكلام المورد فيه ذلك من قبيل الأستعارة التمثيلية ولا نظر فيها إلى تشبيه المفردات بالمفردات

ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r3.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas is reported to understand “glorify in the name of your Lord” as praying in His name, with the preposition omitted; Alusi doubts the report.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن المعنى صل باسم ربك الأعلى كما تقول ابدأ باسم الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r4.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r4.claim: ʿIsam al-Din suggests that “name” means God's trace or effects, which point to Him as names do; Alusi finds this interpretation remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r4.anchor: وقال عصام الدين لا يبعد أن يراد الاسم الأثر أي أثر سبح آثار ربك الأعلى عن النقصان

ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r5.claim: If sabbiḥ means “sanctify,” either an inserted “name” or direct sanctification of names is possible; if it means “say subḥān,” “name” must be inserted, since no one says “glory to the name of my Lord.”
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r5.anchor: وإذا كان معناه قل سبحان كما هو المعروف فيما بينهم فكونه مقحما متعين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r6.speaker: أبي بن كعب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r6.claim: A reading transmitted from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb says “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High,” supporting the interpretation of the command as uttering subḥān.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r6.anchor: ويؤيد هذا قراءة أبي بن كعب كما في خبر سعيد بن منصور وعبد بن حميد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r7.claim: Alusi rejects the claim that the divine name and the named referent are identical, directing readers to his earlier discussion.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r7.anchor: وأما ما قيل من أن الاسم عين المسمى واستدل عليه بهذه الآية ونحوها فهو مما لا يعول عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r8.claim: “Most High” describes God's power and dominion, not a location; alternatively, if it describes the name, that name is exalted above sharing its meaning with any other name.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p103/r8.anchor: والأعلى صفة للرب وأريد بالعلو بالقهر والأقتدار لا بالمكان لاستحالته عليه سبحانه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p396#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p396#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p396#2/r1.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says that when the Prophet recited ‘Glorify the name of your Lord Most High,’ he said ‘Glory to my Lord Most High’; a group of Companions and Successors agree.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p396#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p396#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p396#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p396#2/r2.claim: Some understand the command as declaring God above the descriptions of heretics and treat ‘name’ as an extra word; this supports identifying name and named entity.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p396#2/r2.anchor: وقال قوم: معناه نزه ربك الأعلى عما يصفه به الملحدون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p396#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p396#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p396#2/r3.claim: Others interpret it as honoring the naming of God by remembering him reverently and obeying his commands, taking ism to mean naming or mention.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p396#2/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: نزه تسمية ربك، بأن تذكره وأنت له معظم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p396#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p396#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p396#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas also interprets the command as praying according to the order of the Most High Lord.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p396#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: سبح [اسم ربك الأعلى] (2) أي:

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r1.claim: Glorifying God's name means guarding it against deviant interpretation and applying it to another as though the two were equal; mention الأعلى magnifies Him. One reading says سبحان ربي الأعلى.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r1.anchor: نزه اسمه عن إلحاد فيه بالتأويلات الزائغة وإطلاقه على غيره

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r2.claim: When 69:52 was revealed, the Prophet instructed the companions to use its glorification in bowing; on this verse's revelation he instructed them to use it in prostration.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r2.anchor: لما نزلت { فسبح باسم ربك العظيم } قال عليه الصلاة والسلام اجعلوها في ركوعكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r3.claim: The companions also used supplications in bowing and prostration, saying “O God, to You I bow” and “O God, to You I prostrate.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r3.anchor: وكانوا يقولون في الركوع اللهم لك ركعت وفي السجود اللهم لك سجدت

BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r5.claim: Purification is the glorification commanded at the sura's opening and the good actions that follow from it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r5.anchor: وذلك هو التسبيخ الذي أمر به أول السورة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r8.claim: The purification, remembrance, and prayer reprise the opening's divine traits: removing defects and acquiring perfections; this paired ellipsis links prayer with escape from the greatest fire.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p400/r8.anchor: وكان متخلقا بما ذكر من أخلاق الله في أول السورة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r5.claim: Ending with purification returns to the beginning's glorification and soul-cleansing; God does not leave creation without guidance or create them purposelessly.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p402/r5.anchor: وكان في إتيانه والتذكير به إعلام بأن الله تعالى لم يهمل الخلق

DURR-FULL:v8p479/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p479/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p479/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Surat al-Ala was revealed in Mecca; reports from Ibn al-Zubayr and Aisha likewise place it there.
DURR-FULL:v8p479/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت سورة {سبح} بمكة

DURR-FULL:v8p479/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p479/r2.speaker: البراء بن عازب
