IBNKATHIR:87:1/r7.claim: A report from Ubayy, Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abzā, and ʿĀʾisha says the Prophet recited this sūra, al-Kāfirūn, and al-Ikhlāṣ in witr; ʿĀʾisha adds the two refuge sūras.
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r7.anchor: من حديث أبي بن كعب ، وعبد الله بن عباس ، وعبد الرحمن بن أبزى ، وعائشة أم المؤمنين : أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR:87:1/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r8.speaker: عقبة بن عامر الجهني
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r8.claim: When 87:1 was revealed, the Prophet instructed the Companions to use its glorification in prostration, just as he assigned 56:74 and 56:96 to bowing.
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r8.anchor: سمعت عقبة بن عامر الجهني لما نزلت : { فسبح باسم ربك العظيم }

IBNKATHIR:87:1/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r9.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that when the Prophet recited this verse, he said, “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.”
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس : أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأ : { سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الأعْلَى }

IBNKATHIR:87:1/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r10.speaker: أبو وكيع وشعبة
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r10.claim: Abū Dāwūd notes that Wakiʿ’s marfūʿ version is disputed: Abū Wakiʿ and Shuʿba transmit Ibn ʿAbbās’s wording as mawqūf.
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r10.anchor: رواه أبو وكيع وشعبة ، عن أبي إسحاق ، عن سعيد ، عن ابن عباس ، موقوفا

IBNKATHIR:87:1/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r11.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r11.claim: ʿAlī likewise said “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High” when he recited this verse.
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r11.anchor: عن عبد خير قال : سمعت عليا قرأ

IBNKATHIR:87:1/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās said this glorification at 87:1 and, at the end of 75:40, said “Glory to You indeed, yes.”
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r12.anchor: أن ابن عباس كان إذا قرأ : { سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الأعْلَى } يقول : سبحان ربي الأعلى

IBNKATHIR:87:1/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r13.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r13.claim: Qatāda says it was related that the Prophet said “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High” when reciting the verse.
IBNKATHIR:87:1/r13.anchor: وقال قتادة : { سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الأعْلَى } ذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأها

IBNKATHIR:92:1/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:1/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:92:1/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir recalls the Prophet asking Muʿadh why he had not prayed using al-Aʿlā, al-Shams and al-Layl.
IBNKATHIR:92:1/r2.anchor: قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام لمعاذ :  " فهلا صليت ب "

KASHSHAF:87:1/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:1/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:1/r1.claim: Al-Ala is Meccan and consists of nineteen verses.

KASHSHAF:87:1/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:1/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:1/r2.claim: Glorifying God's name declares Him free of heretical meanings attributed to His names, such as determinism or anthropomorphism.
KASHSHAF:87:1/r2.anchor: تنزيهه عما لا يصح فيه من المعاني التي هي إلحاد في أسمائه

KASHSHAF:87:1/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:1/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:1/r3.claim: Al-Ala is exalted in domination and power, not spatial height or literal establishment on the Throne.
KASHSHAF:87:1/r3.anchor: مثل أن يفسر الأعلى بمعنى العلو الذي هو القهر والاقتدار

KASHSHAF:87:1/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:1/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:1/r4.claim: God's name is protected from casual mention and spoken with humility and reverence.
KASHSHAF:87:1/r4.anchor: وأن يصان عن الابتذال والذكر ، لا على وجه الخشوع والتعظيم

KASHSHAF:87:1/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:1/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:1/r5.claim: Al-Ala may be parsed as an adjective of rabb.
KASHSHAF:87:1/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { الأعلى } صفة للرب

KASHSHAF:87:1/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:1/r6.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF:87:1/r6.claim: Ali reads Subhana rabbi al-aʿla instead of sabbih.
KASHSHAF:87:1/r6.anchor: وقرأ علي رضي الله عنه : سبحان ربي الأعلى

KASHSHAF:87:1/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:1/r7.speaker: النبي
KASHSHAF:87:1/r7.claim: The Prophet directs the command to glorify the great Lord by name for bowing, and this verse for prostration.
KASHSHAF:87:1/r7.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : "  اجعلوها في ركوعكم

KASHSHAF:87:1/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:1/r8.speaker: النبي
KASHSHAF:87:1/r8.claim: The Prophet says to place this glorification in prostration.
KASHSHAF:87:1/r8.anchor: فلما نزل سبح اسم ربك الأعلى قال : "  اجعلوها في سجودكم

KASHSHAF:87:1/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:1/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:1/r9.claim: Their formulas were, in bowing, God, to You I bow, and in prostration, God, to You I prostrate.
KASHSHAF:87:1/r9.anchor: وكانوا يقولون في الركوع : اللهم لك ركعت ، وفي السجود

MAWARDI:87:1/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:1/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
MAWARDI:87:1/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi interpret sabbih as glorify your Lord Most High; ism is an added word intended to exalt the named one, as Labid’s verse illustrates.
MAWARDI:87:1/r2.anchor: عظّم ربك الأعلى ،   قاله ابن عباس والسدي ،   والاسم صلة قصد بها تعظيم المسّمى ،   كما قال لبيد

MAWARDI:87:1/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:1/r3.speaker: الطبري
MAWARDI:87:1/r3.claim: Al-Tabari interprets the command as declaring the Lord’s name too exalted to be given to anyone else.
MAWARDI:87:1/r3.anchor: نزّه اسم ربك عن أن يسمى به أحد سواه ،   ذكره الطبري

MAWARDI:87:1/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:1/r4.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:87:1/r4.claim: Another interpretation is to raise one’s voice in remembrance of the Lord, supported by Jarir’s verse about pilgrims chanting and magnifying God.
MAWARDI:87:1/r4.anchor:
معناه ارفع صوتك بذكر ربك ،   قال جرير :
قَبَحَ الإلهُ وَجوه تَغْلبَ كلّما *** سَبَحَ الحجيجُ وكبّروا تكبيرا

MAWARDI:87:1/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:1/r5.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:87:1/r5.claim: A fourth interpretation is pray to your Lord.

MAWARDI:87:1/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:1/r6.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:87:1/r6.claim: On the prayer interpretation, ism rabbika can mean by your Lord’s command.

MAWARDI:87:1/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:1/r7.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:87:1/r7.claim: It can instead mean by mentioning your Lord at the opening of prayer.
MAWARDI:87:1/r7.anchor: بذكر ربك أن تفتتح به الصلاة

MAWARDI:87:1/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:1/r8.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:87:1/r8.claim: It can also mean keeping the Lord in one’s heart while intending the prayer.
MAWARDI:87:1/r8.anchor: أن تكون ذاكرا لربك بقلبك في نيتك للصلاة

MAWARDI:87:1/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:1/r9.speaker: علي وابن عباس وابن عمر
MAWARDI:87:1/r9.claim: Ali, Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Umar would say Glory be to my Lord Most High when beginning the sura’s recitation, acting on its opening command.
MAWARDI:87:1/r9.anchor: وروي أن عليّاً وابن عباس وابن عمر كانوا إذا افتتحوا قراءة هذه السورة قالوا :  "  سبحان ربي الأعلى  "  امتثالاً لأمره تعالى في ابتدائها

MAWARDI:87:1/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:1/r10.speaker: أبي وابن عمر
MAWARDI:87:1/r10.claim: It is said that Ubay’s reading has Glory be to my Lord Most High in place of the opening words, and Ibn Umar recited it that way.
MAWARDI:87:1/r10.anchor: وقيل إنها في قراءة أُبيّ :  "  سبحان ربي الأعلى  "  وكان ابن عمر يقرؤها كذلك

NASAFI:87:1/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:1/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:1/r1.claim: Sura al-A‘la is Makkan and has nineteen verses.

NASAFI:87:1/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:1/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:1/r2.claim: The command means to declare God’s essence free of what does not befit Him; ‘the Most High’ means exalted in dominion and power, not in spatial location. Alternatively, say ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.’
NASAFI:87:1/r2.anchor: نزه ذاته عما لا يليق به ، والاسم صلة وذلك بأن يفسر الأعلى بمعنى العلو الذي هو القهر والاقتدار

NASAFI:87:1/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:1/r3.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
NASAFI:87:1/r3.claim: When the verse was revealed, the Prophet instructed worshippers to recite it in prostration.
NASAFI:87:1/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث لما نزلت قال عليه السلام

QURTUBI:87:1/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:1/r1.claim: Most call the sura Meccan; al-Dahhak calls it Medinan. It has nineteen verses.
QURTUBI:87:1/r1.anchor: مكية في قول الجمهور . وقال الضحاك : مدنية . وهي تسع عشرة آية

QURTUBI:87:1/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:87:1/r2.claim: The reciter should say “Glory to my Lord, the Most High” after the sura; the Prophet and groups of Companions and Successors did so.
QURTUBI:87:1/r2.anchor: يستحب للقارئ إذا قرأ  " سبح اسم ربك الأعلى "  أن يقول عقبه : سبحان ربي الأعلى . قاله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI:87:1/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r3.speaker: جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه عن جده
QURTUBI:87:1/r3.claim: A report says angel Hizqiyal multiplied his wings and flew for tens of thousands of years without reaching a support of the Throne; he then uttered this glorification, prompting the verse and the Prophet's instruction to say it in prostration. No grading is given.
QURTUBI:87:1/r3.anchor: روى جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه عن جده قال : ( إن لله تعالى ملكا يقال له حزقيائيل

QURTUBI:87:1/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r4.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
QURTUBI:87:1/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi explain sabbih as magnifying the Lord; “name” is an added expression to magnify the one named, as in Labid's line.
QURTUBI:87:1/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والسدي : معنى  " سبح اسم ربك الأعلى "  أي عظم ربك الأعلى

QURTUBI:87:1/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:1/r5.claim: Another explanation is to declare the Lord free of evil and claims made by unbelievers.
QURTUBI:87:1/r5.anchor: وقيل : نزه ربك عن السوء ، وعما يقول فيه الملحدون

QURTUBI:87:1/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r6.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI:87:1/r6.claim: Al-Tabari says to purify the Lord's name from being used to name anyone else.
QURTUBI:87:1/r6.anchor: وذكر الطبري أن المعنى نزه اسم ربك عن أن تسمي به أحدا سواه

QURTUBI:87:1/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:1/r7.claim: Another view means naming and mentioning God only with reverence and respect; al-Qurtubi prefers that the name is the one named.
QURTUBI:87:1/r7.anchor: وقيل : نزه تسمية ربك وذكرك إياه ، أن تذكره إلا وأنت خاشع معظم

QURTUBI:87:1/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:1/r8.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers that “name” is the named entity, not the act of naming; worshippers say “Glory to my Lord,” not “Glory to the name of my Lord.”
QURTUBI:87:1/r8.anchor: وجعلوا الاسم بمعنى التسمية ، والأولى أن يكون الاسم هو المسمى

QURTUBI:87:1/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r9.speaker: نافع عن ابن عمر
QURTUBI:87:1/r9.claim: Nafi transmits Ibn Umar's instruction not to say “in God's name,” since God's name itself is Most High.
QURTUBI:87:1/r9.anchor: روى نافع عن ابن عمر قال : لا تقل على اسم الله ، فإن اسم الله هو الأعلى

QURTUBI:87:1/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r10.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI:87:1/r10.claim: Abu Salih transmits Ibn Abbas's explanation: pray by the command of your Most High Lord, saying “Glory to your Lord, the Most High.”
QURTUBI:87:1/r10.anchor: روى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس : صل بأمر ربك الأعلى

QURTUBI:87:1/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r11.speaker: علي وابن عباس وابن عمرو وابن الزبير وأبو موسى وابن مسعود
QURTUBI:87:1/r11.claim: These Companions began reciting the sura with “Glory to my Lord, the Most High”; al-Qurtubi recommends following them and rejects treating the phrase as Quranic text.
QURTUBI:87:1/r11.anchor: وروي عن علي رضي الله عنه ، وابن عباس وابن عمرو وابن الزبير وأبي موسى وعبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنهم

QURTUBI:87:1/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r12.speaker: أبي بن كعب
QURTUBI:87:1/r12.claim: “Glory to my Lord, the Most High” is reported as Ubayy's reading, and Ibn Umar recited it so; al-Qurtubi denies it is Quranic text.
QURTUBI:87:1/r12.anchor: وقيل : إنها في قراءة أبي : " سبحان ربي الأعلى " . وكان ابن عمر يقرؤها كذلك

QURTUBI:87:1/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:87:1/r13.claim: A report says the Prophet said the glorification when reciting the sura. No grading is stated.
QURTUBI:87:1/r13.anchor: وفي الحديث : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قرأها قال : [ سبحان ربي الأعلى ]

QURTUBI:87:1/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r14.speaker: عقبة بن عامر الجهني
QURTUBI:87:1/r14.claim: Uqba ibn Amir reports the Prophet's instruction to say the glorification in prostration.
QURTUBI:87:1/r14.anchor: وعن عقبة بن عامر الجهني قال : لما نزلت  " سبح اسم ربك الأعلى "

QURTUBI:87:1/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r15.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI:87:1/r15.claim: Al-Anbari reports Ali reciting the verse in prayer and saying “Glory to my Lord, the Most High”; when challenged, he said he merely did what he was commanded.
QURTUBI:87:1/r15.anchor: قرأ علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام في الصلاة

QURTUBI:87:1/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:1/r16.claim: The practice of saying “Glory to my Lord,” rather than “Glory to the name of my Lord,” indicates that the name is the named entity.
QURTUBI:87:1/r16.anchor: وهذا كله يدل على أن الاسم هو المسمى

QURTUBI:87:1/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r17.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:1/r17.claim: One report says Michael was the first to utter “Glory to my Lord, the Most High.”
QURTUBI:87:1/r17.anchor: وقيل : إن أول من قال [ سبحان ربي الأعلى ] ميكائيل عليه السلام

QURTUBI:87:1/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r18.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:87:1/r18.claim: A report has the Prophet ask Gabriel about the reward; Gabriel says it outweighs the Throne, Chair, and mountains, earns forgiveness and Paradise, and Michael will visit and intercede. No grading is supplied.
QURTUBI:87:1/r18.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لجبريل : ( يا جبريل أخبرني بثواب من قال : سبحان ربي الأعلى

QURTUBI:87:1/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r19.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI:87:1/r19.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the command as praying to the Most High Lord.
QURTUBI:87:1/r19.anchor: وقال الحسن : " سبح اسم ربك الأعلى " أي صل لربك الأعلى

QURTUBI:87:1/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r20.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:1/r20.claim: Another gloss says to pray using God's names, unlike polytheists who worshipped by whistling and clapping.
QURTUBI:87:1/r20.anchor: وقل : أي صل بأسماء الله ، لا كما يصلي المشركون بالمكاء والتصدية

QURTUBI:87:1/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r21.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:1/r21.claim: Another interpretation is to raise one's voice in remembrance of the Lord.

QURTUBI:87:1/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:1/r22.speaker: جرير
QURTUBI:87:1/r22.claim: Jarir's line about pilgrims glorifying and magnifying God illustrates sabbaha for devotional praise.
QURTUBI:87:1/r22.anchor: قال جرير : قبح الإله وجوه تغلب كلما

QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas says to respond to al-Aʿlā with Subḥāna rabbī al-aʿlā and to the end of this sūra with Subḥānaka Allāhumma balā, whether leading prayer or not.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:36-40/r14.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: من قرأ سبح اسم ربك الأعلى

RAZI:87:1/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r1.claim: Rāzī gives two readings of the command: sanctify God’s name, or treat “name” as an added expression and sanctify God Himself.

RAZI:87:1/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r2.claim: On the first reading, the command may forbid applying God’s name to others, as polytheists named an idol al-Lāt and Musaylima called himself the Merciful of Yamāma.
RAZI:87:1/r2.anchor: نزه اسم ربك عن أن تسمي به غيره

RAZI:87:1/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r3.claim: Another reading forbids explaining divine names in ways that imply bodily attributes: “the Most High” is not spatial height, and istiwāʾ is not settling.
RAZI:87:1/r3.anchor: أن لا يفسر أسماءه بما لا يصح ثبوته في حقه سبحانه نحو أن يفسر الأعلى بالعلو في المكان

RAZI:87:1/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r4.claim: The divine name must be protected from casual mention without reverence, humility, or understanding of its meaning.
RAZI:87:1/r4.anchor: أن يصان عن الابتذال والذكر لا على وجه الخشوع والتعظيم

RAZI:87:1/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r5.claim: The command can mean glorify God through the names He revealed and authorized.
RAZI:87:1/r5.anchor: أي مجده بأسمائه التي أنزلتها عليك

RAZI:87:1/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r6.claim: This reading also means praying by God’s revealed name, unlike the polytheists’ clapping and whistling, and using only names established by revelation.
RAZI:87:1/r6.anchor: لا كما يصلي المشركون بالمكاء والتصدية

RAZI:87:1/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r7.speaker: الفراء
RAZI:87:1/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ sees no difference in meaning between “sanctify the name of your Lord” and “sanctify by the name of your Lord.”

RAZI:87:1/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r8.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI:87:1/r8.claim: Al-Wāḥidī distinguishes the forms: the one with bi- glorifies God by His name, while the other purifies the name itself from evil.
RAZI:87:1/r8.anchor: قال الواحدي : وبينهما فرق لأن معنى

RAZI:87:1/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r9.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI:87:1/r9.claim: Abū Muslim takes “name” here to mean attribute, as in the verse about God’s beautiful names.
RAZI:87:1/r9.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : المراد من الاسم ههنا الصفة

RAZI:87:1/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r10.claim: A second major reading, favored by a group of careful scholars, treats “name” as an added expression: the intended command is to glorify the Lord.
RAZI:87:1/r10.anchor: أما على الوجه الثاني وهو أن يكون الاسم صلة ويكون المعنى سبح ربك وهو اختيار جمع من المحققين

RAZI:87:1/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r11.claim: Arabic convention mentions the name or remembrance of an exalted person instead of naming that person directly.
RAZI:87:1/r11.anchor: ولكن المذكور إذا كان في غاية العظمة لا يذكر هو بل يذكر اسمه

RAZI:87:1/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r12.speaker: لبيد
RAZI:87:1/r12.claim: Labīd’s phrase “the name of Peace be upon you” uses “name of Peace” to mean Peace itself.
RAZI:87:1/r12.anchor:
وقال لبيد :
إلى الحول ثم اسم السلام عليكما

RAZI:87:1/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r13.claim: One meaning of glorifying God is avoiding conduct toward unbelievers that provokes them to insult God.
RAZI:87:1/r13.anchor: ولا تسبوا الذين يدعون من دون الله فيسبوا الله عدوا بغير علم

RAZI:87:1/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r14.claim: Glorifying God in His essence means believing He is neither a substance nor an accident.
RAZI:87:1/r14.anchor: أما في ذاته فأن يعتقد أنها ليست من الجواهر والأعراض

RAZI:87:1/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r15.claim: Glorifying God in His attributes means believing they are neither originated, finite, nor deficient.
RAZI:87:1/r15.anchor: وأما في صفاته ، فأن يعتقد أنها ليست محدثة ولا متناهية ولا ناقصة

RAZI:87:1/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r16.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r16.claim: In His acts, glorification means affirming God’s absolute ownership, which leaves no one entitled to object to His decisions.
RAZI:87:1/r16.anchor: وأما في أفعاله فأن يعتقد أنه مالك مطلق

RAZI:87:1/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r17.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI:87:1/r17.claim: The Muʿtazilites define glorifying God’s acts as affirming that everything He does is good and right, and that He neither does nor approves evil.
RAZI:87:1/r17.anchor: وقالت المعتزلة هو أن يعتقد أن كل ما فعله فهو صواب حسن

RAZI:87:1/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r18.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r18.claim: Rāzī’s position is that God should be named only by names established through revelation.
RAZI:87:1/r18.anchor: أما في أسمائه فأن لا يذكر سبحانه إلا بالأسماء التي ورد التوقيف بها

RAZI:87:1/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r19.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI:87:1/r19.claim: The Muʿtazilites permit any name that suggests no deficiency, whether or not revelation authorized it.
RAZI:87:1/r19.anchor: وأما عند المعتزلة فهو أن لا يذكر إلا بالأسماء التي لا توهم نقصا بوجه من الوجوه

RAZI:87:1/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r20.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r20.claim: Rāzī says God imposes duties for no benefit to Himself, purely by ownership; the Muʿtazilite view is that duties serve people’s interests.
RAZI:87:1/r20.anchor: بل إما لمحض المالكية على ما هو قولنا ، أو لرعاية مصالح العباد على ما [ هو ] قول المعتزلة

RAZI:87:1/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r21.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r21.claim: Some have used this verse to argue that a name is identical with the named entity.
RAZI:87:1/r21.anchor: من الناس من تمسك بهذه الآية في أن الاسم نفس المسمى

RAZI:87:1/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r22.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r22.claim: Rāzī says the dispute is poorly framed: if “name” means the word and “named” the entity they differ; if both mean the entity, their identity is tautological.
RAZI:87:1/r22.anchor: فالعاقل لا يمكنه أن يقول : الاسم هو المسمى

RAZI:87:1/r23.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r23.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r23.claim: He suggests the confusion may come from “name” itself being a noun denoting a timeless meaning, leading later scholars to generalize an earlier formulation.

RAZI:87:1/r24.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r24.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r24.claim: An argument for identity says people do not say “Glory be to the name of God”; therefore this command means glorify the Lord, who is Himself called by a name.
RAZI:87:1/r24.anchor: والرب أيضا اسم فلو كان غير المسمى

RAZI:87:1/r25.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r25.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r25.claim: Rāzī rejects that argument as weak because the command can sanctify the name itself, use “name” as an addition, or mean glorify God by His names.
RAZI:87:1/r25.anchor: واعلم أن هذا الاستدلال ضعيف لما بينا في المسألة الأولى

RAZI:87:1/r26.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r26.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
RAZI:87:1/r26.claim: A report from ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir says the Prophet instructed worshippers to use the verse about the Great Lord in bowing and this verse in prostration.
RAZI:87:1/r26.anchor: روى عن عقبة بن عامر أنه لما نزل

RAZI:87:1/r27.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r27.speaker: النبي
RAZI:87:1/r27.claim: Reports say the Prophet recited “Glory be to my Lord, the Great” in bowing and “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High” in prostration.
RAZI:87:1/r27.anchor: أنه عليه السلام كان يقول : في ركوعه : «سبحان ربي العظيم

RAZI:87:1/r28.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r28.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r28.claim: Some scholars infer from these reports that the command means to pray using the Lord’s name; they also cite the exegetes’ agreement that 30:17 gives prayer times.
RAZI:87:1/r28.anchor: من العلماء من قال : إن هذه الأحاديث تدل

RAZI:87:1/r29.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r29.speaker: علي
RAZI:87:1/r29.claim: ʿAlī and Ibn ʿUmar read the command as “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High,” followed by “who created and proportioned”; the wording supplies the commanded glorification.
RAZI:87:1/r29.anchor: قرأ علي عليه السلام وابن عمر : ( سبحان ربي الأعلى

RAZI:87:1/r30.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r30.speaker: المجسمة
RAZI:87:1/r30.claim: The anthropomorphists cite “the Most High” to argue that God is elevated in a physical direction.
RAZI:87:1/r30.anchor: تمسكت المجسمة في إثبات العلو بالمكان بقوله :

RAZI:87:1/r31.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r31.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r31.claim: Rāzī rejects spatial elevation: a finite God would have a direction above Him, while an infinite body either has impossible infinite dimensions or is composite and contingent.
RAZI:87:1/r31.anchor: والحق أن العلو بالجهة على الله تعالى محال

RAZI:87:1/r32.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r32.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r32.claim: The surrounding context concerns praise: remoteness from the world does not merit praise, while supreme power and unique creation do.
RAZI:87:1/r32.anchor: أما قبل الآية فلأن العلو عبارة عن كونه في غاية البعد عن العالم

RAZI:87:1/r33.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r33.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r33.claim: The next description, “who created and proportioned,” confirms that “Most High” refers to power rather than physical direction.
RAZI:87:1/r33.anchor: والخالقية تناسب العلو بحسب القدرة لا العلو بحسب الجهة

RAZI:87:1/r34.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r34.speaker: الملحدون
RAZI:87:1/r34.claim: Some skeptics claim that “the Great” and “the Most High” imply two lords, one greater than the other.
RAZI:87:1/r34.anchor: من الملحدين من قال : بأن القرآن مشعر

RAZI:87:1/r35.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r35.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r35.claim: Rāzī answers that reason establishes one Creator, and this verse never says God is higher than another lord.
RAZI:87:1/r35.anchor: لما دلت الدلائل على أن الصانع تعالى واحد سقط هذا السؤال

RAZI:87:1/r36.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r36.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r36.claim: “The Most High” can mean that God’s majesty, favors, and claims surpass human knowledge, praise, gratitude, and obedience.
RAZI:87:1/r36.anchor: أنه تعالى أعلى وأجل وأعظم من كل ما يصفه به الواصفون

RAZI:87:1/r37.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r37.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r37.claim: Alternatively, the title signals God’s freedom from every defect and His superiority over all things in dominion, sovereignty, and power.
RAZI:87:1/r37.anchor: أن قوله { الأعلى } تنبيه على استحقاق الله التنزيه

RAZI:87:1/r38.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r38.speaker: author
RAZI:87:1/r38.claim: A third option is that al-aʿlā simply means al-ʿālī, just as al-akbar can mean al-kabīr.
RAZI:87:1/r38.anchor: أن يكون المراد بالأعلى العالي كما أن المراد بالأكبر الكبير

RAZI:87:1/r39.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r39.speaker: النبي
RAZI:87:1/r39.claim: A report says the Prophet loved this sūra and said that anyone who knew its merit would recite it sixteen times.
RAZI:87:1/r39.anchor: لو علم الناس علم سبح اسم ربك الأعلى

RAZI:87:1/r40.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:1/r40.speaker: عائشة
RAZI:87:1/r40.claim: ʿĀʾisha heard a Bedouin leading prayer with a distorted improvised recitation about pregnancy and childbirth, then rebuked him and his companions.
RAZI:87:1/r40.anchor: أن عائشة مرت بأعرابي يصلي بأصحابه فقرأ : ( سبح اسم ربك الأعلى

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r1.claim: The divine name is precious: its seeker finds it, its petitioner praises it, and its seeker comes to know it and receive divine gentleness.

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r2.claim: Intimacy with God makes one unwilling to oppose Him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r2.anchor: ومن عرفه لاطفه ، فإذا وجد لطفه

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r3.claim: Glorify God through knowledge of His names and swim inwardly in His exaltedness, extracting its jewels to adorn praise.

FARRA:v3p256/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p256/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p256/r1.claim: Both forms, 'glorify the name of your Lord' and 'glorify by the name of your Lord,' occur in Arabic usage.
FARRA:v3p256/r1.anchor: كل ذلك قد جاء وهو من كلام العرب

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.claim: The preceding sūrah urges the Prophet to wait: persistent deniers receive only temporary respite under God's practice, and cannot escape His grasp.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.anchor: Sūrah al-Ṭāriq, the previous sūrah ended on urging the Prophet (sws) to show patience and to wait for the decision of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.claim: This sūrah shifts its primary address from stubborn Quraysh to the Prophet and, over at least ten following sūrahs, dispels his preaching fears in varied ways.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.anchor: while ignoring these stubborn elements from among the Quraysh, the Prophet (sws) is addressed directly and given glad tidings

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r3.claim: Verses 1–5 direct the Prophet to glorify God, whose attributes show that creation and human physical and intellectual capacities mature gradually.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p272/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p272/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p272/r1.claim: Tasbīḥ means declaring the Almighty free of anything inconsistent with His majesty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p272/r1.anchor: serves to absolve the Almighty of all things which are against His majesty

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r1.claim: True comprehension of God grounds knowledge, cognizance, power, and belief; errors in it lead to Satanic misguidance and weaken faith, trust, satisfaction, and perseverance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r1.anchor: man is led away from true knowledge

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r2.claim: God's remembrance comforts the heart, strengthens it, and keeps it content and on the right path.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r2.anchor: surely in the remembrance of God all hearts are comforted

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r3.claim: Prayer, especially tahajjud, is the highest form of tasbīḥ; continuous remembrance through daily routines sustains spiritual life and guards against Satan.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r3.anchor: is the prayer, especially the tahajjud prayer

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p273/r4.claim: The Prophet is commanded to use tasbīḥ comprehensively as a source of fortitude and perseverance.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r1.claim: Sabbih means declaring God free of defects; the apparent reading directs glorification to God's name, excluding its use for idols, which even more strongly entails God's transcendence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r1.anchor: سبح: نزه عن النقائص، اسم ربك: الظاهر أن التنزيه يقع على الاسم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r2.claim: Some take the name to mean the named one; another view says God's name should only be mentioned reverently.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r2.anchor: وقيل: الاسم هنا بمعنى المسمى. وقيل: معناه نزه اسم الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the command as praying in the name of the Most High Lord, with a preposition omitted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: المعنى صل باسم ربك الأعلى، كما تقول: ابدأ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r4.claim: A report says the Prophet directed worshippers to say the Most High Lord's glorification in prostration, following the direction for the Great Lord in bowing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r4.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «اجعلوها في ركوعكم»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r5.claim: Al-Aʿlā can modify Lord in genitive or name in accusative; the latter fails if alladhī khalaq is an adjective of Lord because another adjective intervenes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r5.anchor: الأعلى يصح أن يكون صفة لربك، وأن يكون صفة لاسم فيكون منصوبا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r6.claim: If alladhī khalaq is instead a predicate of an omitted subject or an accusative of praise, al-Aʿlā can modify the name.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r6.anchor: فإن لم يجعل الذي صفة لربك، بل ترفعه على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r1.speaker: الملوي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r1.claim: The surah is also called Sabbiḥ; al-Malawi says the Prophet liked it for its abundance of learning and benefits.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r1.anchor: وتسمى سبح قال الملوي : وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يحبها لكثرة ما اشتملت عليه من العلوم والخيرات

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r2.claim: The surah's purpose is to affirm God's transcendence above every deficiency, including haste, inability to resurrect, purposeless creation, false speech, or speech humans can imitate.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r2.anchor: إيجاب التنزيه للأعلى سبحانه وتعالى عن أن يلحق ساحة عظمته شيء من شوائب النقص

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r3.claim: The surah al-Tariq alluded to these denials generally, while this surah explains them in detail.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r3.anchor: كما أذنت بذلك الطارق مجملا وشرحته هذه مفصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r4.claim: The basmala describes God as possessing all exaltedness, whose generosity creates, nurtures, and provides for every creature.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r4.anchor: فلا نقص يلحقه { الرحمن } الذي عم جوده

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r5.claim: God's mercy gives His adherents both the obligation and the ability, through guidance, to obey.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#s087/r5.anchor: الذي من كان من حزبه فإنه يلزمه الطاعة وييسرها له ويوفقه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r1.claim: The preceding surah's call to wait implies that God is free of the defect of haste; its denial that revelation is frivolous answers another accusation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r1.anchor: بالإمهال النهي عن الاستعجال الذي هو منزه عنه لكونه نقصا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r2.claim: God commands His perfected Messenger to glorify His name because the Messenger alone knows how to do so with full understanding.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r2.anchor: أمر أكمل خلقة رسوله المنزل عليه هذا القرآن صلى الله عليه وسلم بتنزيه اسمه لأنه وحده العالم بذلك حق علمه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r3.claim: Protecting God's name from idolatrous invocation or irreverent use entails even greater reverence for God Himself.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r3.anchor: إذا نزه اسمه عن أن يدعو به وثنا أو غيره أو يضعه في غير ما يليق به

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r4.claim: Glorification, especially declaring God free of impossibilities, comes before affirming attributes; the surah accordingly sets out theology before prophethood.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r4.anchor: شارحا لأصول الدين مقدما للإلهيات التي هي النهايات

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r5.claim: Beginning with God's essence, attributes, self-subsistence, and acts before prophethood cures ignorant imitation and arrogant denial and leads to obedience.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r6.claim: Sabbiḥ means to glorify and clear God with exceptionally strong, emphatic purification.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r6.anchor: أي نزه وبرئ تنزيها وتبرئة عظمتين جدا قويتين شديدتين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r7.claim: The Lord is the benefactor who creates the person perfectly and raises him through the finest qualities to dignity and beauty.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r7.anchor: المحسن إليك بعد إيجادك على صفة الكمال بتربيتك على أحسن الخلال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r8.claim: Human well-being needs a powerful patron, an exemplar, and an ideal way; the reported confession names God, Muhammad, and Islam in these roles.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r8.anchor: رضيت بالله ربا وبمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم نبيا ورسولا وبالإسلام دينا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r9.claim: Al-Aʿla means supreme in rank, not location, and wholly free of defect, distortive interpretations of His names, or irreverent mention.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r9.anchor: الذي له وصف الأعلوية في المكانة لا المكان على الإطلاق عن كل شائبة نقص

BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r10.claim: The opening glorification formula develops across four forms: the verbal noun in al-Isra, past tense in three surahs, present tense in two, then the imperative here.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p393#2/r10.anchor: ابتداء سورة الإسراء التي هي سورة الإحسان

DURR-FULL:v8p482/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r1.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's reading is said to match the reading just mentioned.
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r1.anchor: كذلك هي قراءة أبي بن كعب

DURR-FULL:v8p482/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r2.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr recited the verse and then said Glorified is my Lord, the Most High, during prayer.
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الزبير أنه قرأ {سبح اسم ربك الأعلى} فقال: سبحان ربي الأعلى وهو في الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v8p482/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak read it in this manner and instructed anyone who recites it to say Glorified is my Lord, the Most High.
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك أنه كان يقرؤها كذلك

DURR-FULL:v8p482/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r4.claim: Qatada reports that the Prophet said Glorified is my Lord, the Most High when he recited this verse.
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قال: ذكر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأها قال: سبحان ربي الأعلى

DURR-FULL:v8p482/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r5.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r5.claim: Umar would say Glorified is my Lord, the Most High after reciting the verse.
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r5.anchor: عن عمر أنه كان إذا قرأ {سبح اسم ربك الأعلى} قال: سبحان ربي الأعلى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r1.claim: The surah has nineteen verses by unanimous agreement among the verse counters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r1.anchor: وعدد آيها تسع عشرة آية باتفاق أهل العدد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r2.claim: Its purposes include glorifying God and indicating His oneness through His unique creation of humans and earthly sustenance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r2.anchor: تنزيه الله تعالى والإشارة إلى وحدانيته لانفراده بخلق الإنسان وخلق ما في الأرض مما فيه بقاؤه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r1.claim: Sabbiḥ means glorify and sanctify God, declaring Him free of defects, other gods, and the claims of polytheists.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r1.anchor: بمعنى نزه وقدس وقل سبحانه عن النقائص والغير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r2.claim: The word ism can refer to its bearer, making it virtually redundant here, or to the act and form of naming itself.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r2.anchor: يراد به المسمى، ويأتي في مواضع يراد به التسمية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r3.claim: The verse can mean glorify the Lord Himself, or protect His name from being applied to an idol; al-Aʿla may modify either the name or the Lord.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r3.anchor: وهذه الآية تحتمل هذا الوجه الأول، وتحتمل أن يراد بالاسم التسمية نفسها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r4.claim: According to al-Tabari, Ibn Umar and Ali read the verse as Glorified is my Lord, the Most High, as in Ubayy's codex.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r4.anchor: وذكر الطبري أن ابن عمر وعليا قرآ هذه السورة: «سبحان ربي الأعلى»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r5.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r5.claim: Abu Musa al-Ashari, Ibn al-Zubayr, and Malik ibn Dinar are also reported to read it as Glorified is my Lord, the Most High.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r5.anchor: وهي قراءة أبي موسى الأشعري وابن الزبير ومالك بن أبي دينار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet said Glorified is my Lord, the Most High upon reciting the verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#2/r6.anchor: وروى ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأ هذه الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r1.claim: Some say the command means to mention God's name only while reverent and humble.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r1.anchor: وقال قوم: معنى سبح اسم ربك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the phrase as pray in the name of your Lord, with the preposition omitted as in begin in God's name.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس معنى الآية: صل باسم ربك الأعلى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r16.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r16.claim: Ibn Masʿud, Ibn Amir, and Ibn al-Zubayr also used to say Glorified is my Lord, the Most High.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r16.anchor: وكان ابن مسعود وابن عامر وابن الزبير يفعلون ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r17.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r17.claim: When the verse was revealed, the Prophet instructed believers to include its glorification in prostration.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r17.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «اجعلوها في سجودكم»

JISHUMI:v10p7372/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r1.claim: The surah follows the preceding warning of unbelievers with God’s attributes and power to do whatever He wills.
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r1.anchor:
ما يشاء.
(بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم)
قوله تعالى:

JISHUMI:v10p7372/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r3.claim: Tasbīḥ declares God free of deficiencies and evil, affirms His exalted attributes, and describes His acts as wise and good rather than futile.
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r3.anchor: التسبيح: التنزيه لله عما لا يليق به من صفات النقص وأفعال القبيح، ويوصف بصفات التعظيم

JISHUMI:v10p7372/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r4.claim: Al-aʿlā means exalted in sovereignty and power; this does not imply a place above creation.
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r4.anchor: ومعناه: عال بسلطانه وقدرته، وكل شيء دونه، وهم في سلطانه، ولا يقتضي ذلك مكانا

JISHUMI:v10p7372/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r5.speaker: الفرزدق
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r5.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s verse uses loftiness for strength and honor, illustrating the commentary’s non-spatial sense of elevation.
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r5.anchor: قال الفرزدق: إن الذي سمك السماء بنى لنا

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r5.claim: Al-aʿlā can grammatically modify ism in the accusative or rabb in the genitive.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r5.anchor: (الأعلى) يحتمل أن يكون نصبا نعتا للاسم، ويحتمل أن يكون جرا نعتا للرب.

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r8.claim: They explain the command as saying, “Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.”
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r8.anchor: سبح اسم ربك قيل: سبحان ربي الأعلى، عن ابن عباس، وقتادة.

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r9.claim: Other explanations are to reserve God’s name for Him, reject the pagans’ descriptions, or purify His attributes; Abu Muslim takes name as attributes.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r9.anchor: وقيل: نزه اسم ربك أن تسمي به سواه، وقيل: نزه ربك عما يصفه به المشركون

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r10.claim: A further explanation from Ibn Abbas is to pray using the name of the Lord.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r10.anchor: وقيل: صل باسم ربك، عن ابن عباس،

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r11.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r11.claim: Abu Muslim says name means attribute, so the command is to declare God’s attributes free of what is unfitting.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r11.anchor: وقيل: الاسم الصفة أي: نزه صفاته عما لا يليق به، عن أبي مسلم.

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r12.claim: Another explanation is to glorify God by mentioning His Most High name; the adjective may modify the name or God Himself.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r12.anchor: وقيل: سبح الله بذكر اسمه الأعلى، والأعلى من صفة الاسم، وقيل: من صفة الله

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r13.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r13.claim: Abu Ali says the name is mentioned while its referent is intended, as in the expression “the name of peace be upon you both.”
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r13.anchor: وقيل: ذكر الاسم وأراد به المسمى، أي: نزهه، كقوله: ثم اسم السلام عليكما عن أبي علي.

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r14.claim: Another view calls for choosing a good name because a good name indicates good attributes and deeds.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r14.anchor: وقيل: حسن التسمية؛ لأن حسن الاسم يدل على حسن الصفات وحسن الأفعال.

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r15.claim: Al-aʿlā may mean the all-powerful, unmatched in power and dominant over everyone, or may modify the name whose names are all supreme.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r15.anchor: الأعلى قيل: القادر الذي لا قادر أقدر منه، القاهر لكل أحد، وقيل: الأعلى من نعت الاسم

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r16.claim: Another explanation makes God uniquely deserving of His attributes and beyond the attributes of created beings.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r16.anchor: وأن يستحق صفاته غيره، فيجل عن صفات المحدثين من أن يشبهه أحد

MUQATIL:87:1-7/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r1.speaker: مقاتل
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r1.claim: The command means to purify the name of the Most High Lord from shirk by affirming that there is no god but God.
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r1.anchor: قوله: { سبح اسم ربك } [آية: 1] يقول سبحانه: نزه اسم ربك الأعلى، يقول: نزهه من الشرك

RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r1.claim: Because complete glorification includes reciting the Qur’an God revealed, Muhammad rehearsed it from fear of forgetting; this verse removes that fear.
RAZI-FULL:v31p128/r1.anchor: وعلم محمدا عليه السلام أن ذلك التسبيح لا يتم ولا يكمل إلا بقراءة ما أنزله الله تعالى عليه من القرآن

STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r1.speaker: majority
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r1.claim: Most commentators date al-Aʿlā early Makkan; it is often placed eighth chronologically, after al-Takwīr.
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r1.anchor: the majority maintain that it is early Makkan

STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r3.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r3.claim: Another view holds the whole surah Makkan, since it may refer to the rituals before they were formally instituted.
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r3.anchor: Others say that it can still refer to these ritual practices

STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r4.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r4.claim: The Prophet is said to recommend surahs 87 and 88 for the evening prayer and often recited them at both Eids and Friday prayer.
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r4.anchor: The Prophet is said to have recommended reciting Sūrahs 87 and 88 for the evening prayer

STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r5.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r5.claim: The Prophet is also said to advise reciting the surah while prostrating.
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r5.anchor: advised his followers to recite it while in prostration

STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r6.speaker: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r6.claim: In Shiite tradition, ʿAlī says one who recites it has in effect recited the Quran and scriptures of Moses and Abraham; its blessing merits daily recitation.
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r6.anchor: according to Imam ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, if people knew what a blessing al-Aʿlā has

STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r7.claim: The surah moves from glorification and encouragement to contrasting hearers, rebuking worldly preference, and affirming continuity with earlier revelation.
STUDYQURAN:87:intro/r7.anchor: It concludes with a sharp rebuke of those who prefer this world (vv. 16–17)

TABATABAI:87:1-19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r1.claim: The relation of the divine name to Lord and direct address supports avoiding speech that conflicts with God's self-designation.
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r1.anchor: الإسراء 46. وفي إضافة الاسم إلى الرب والرب إلى ضمير الخطاب

TABATABAI:87:1-19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r2.claim: Al-Aʿlā means the Lord is higher than all and overpowers everything, explaining why His name should be glorified.
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r2.anchor: وهو الذي يعلو كل عال ويقهر كل شيء صفة { ربك } دون الاسم

TABATABAI:87:1-19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r3.claim: A view attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās reads the command as saying ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.’
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r3.anchor: وقيل معنى { سبح اسم ربك الأعلى } قل سبحان ربي الأعلى كما عن ابن عباس

TABATABAI:87:1-19/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r4.claim: Another view takes ‘name’ as ‘the named one,’ commanding God be declared free of unworthy attributes and acts.
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r4.anchor: وقيل المراد بالاسم المسمى والمعنى نزهه تعالى عن كل ما لا يليق

TABATABAI:87:1-19/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r5.speaker: لبيد
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r5.claim: A view treats mention of the name as honoring the named person, citing Labīd's use of ‘the name of peace.’
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r5.anchor: واستشهد عليه بقول لبيد، إلى الحول ثم اسم السلام عليكما

TABATABAI:87:1-19/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r6.claim: Another view requires reverence in interpreting, applying, and uttering God's names.
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r6.anchor: ولا يطلقه على غيره تعالى إذا كان مختصا كاسم الجلالة ولا يتلفظ به

TABATABAI:87:1-19/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r7.claim: The broader explanation best fits the context of preparing the Prophet for reminder and proclamation.
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r7.anchor: وما قدمناه من المعنى أوسع وأشمل وأنسب لسياق قوله الآتي { سنقرئك فلا تنسى }

TABATABAI:87:1-19/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r8.claim: The surah purifies the Prophet's speech from overt or subtle shirk, then promises preserved recitation and ease before commanding reminder.
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r8.anchor: فبدئ أولا بإصلاح كلامه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وتجريده عن كل ما يشعر بجلي الشرك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r1.claim: The command declares the Lord free of evil; another view takes it as saying ‘Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.’
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r1.anchor: { سبح اسم ربك الأعلى } نزه ذات ربك من السوء. وقيل: معناه: قل
